name: universal properties
statement:
**Observation I.4 (universal properties).** [Obs] In $\mathsf{Meth}(\Theta,\theta_0)$:

(a) the frozen model $(\mathrm{pt},*,\theta_0)$ is initial, and full fine-tuning $(\Theta,\theta_0,\mathrm{id})$ is terminal. The unique morphism $M\to$ Full FT is $\rho_M$ itself.

(b) If the fibre product $Q_M\times_\Theta Q_N$ exists in $\mathbf{Diff}$, it is the product $M\times N$. It exists, for instance, when the set-level fibre product is an embedded submanifold of $Q_M\times Q_N$: a clean intersection, or linear/affine $\rho$'s as in Prop I.8(a). Transversality $\rho_M\pitchfork\rho_N$ is never the reason when $\lvert M\rvert+\lvert N\rvert<\dim\Theta$, since at $(q_0,q_0')$ it would force $\lvert M\rvert+\lvert N\rvert\ge\dim\Theta$. In $\mathbf{Set}$ the fibre product always exists and $\mathrm{Im}(M\times N)=\mathrm{Im}\,M\cap\mathrm{Im}\,N$. Whenever the product exists in $\mathsf{Meth}$, its underlying set is this set-level fibre product, so the image identity holds in every case. The product can fail to exist: on $\Theta=\mathbb R$ ($1\times1$ matrices), $\mathrm{LoRA}_1\times\text{Frozen}$ would have the cross $\{BA=0\}\subset\mathbb R^2$ as underlying set, and no manifold structure on it represents smooth maps into the cross. Both axes would have to lift smoothly through the point over the origin, which forces rank $2$ there.

(c) $\mathrm{Im}$ is a functor to the poset of subsets of $\Theta$ containing $\theta_0$. Conversely, $\mathrm{Im}\,M\subseteq\mathrm{Im}\,N$ yields a morphism of the set-level slice $\mathbf{Set}_*/(\Theta,\theta_0)$, but not necessarily a smooth one. Take $\rho_M(t)=t$ and $\rho_N(u)=u^3$ on $\mathbb R$, pointed at $0$: the images agree, yet no smooth $h:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfies $\rho_N\circ h=\mathrm{id}$, i.e. $h(t)^3=t$.
proof:
*Proof.* (a) The only pointed map $\mathrm{pt}\to Q$ is $*\mapsto q_0$, and it lies over $\Theta$ because $\rho(q_0)=\theta_0$. A morphism into the terminal object must satisfy $\mathrm{id}\circ h=\rho_M$.

(b) Products in a pointed slice are pullbacks in $\mathbf{Diff}_*$. The forgetful functor $\mathbf{Diff}_*\to\mathbf{Diff}$ creates limits, since $\mathbf{Diff}_*$ is the coslice $\mathrm{pt}/\mathbf{Diff}$, and the induced map out of a pointed test object is pointed because its components are. Smooth maps landing in an embedded submanifold are smooth into it, which gives the sufficient condition. Transversality at $(q_0,q_0')$ means $d\rho_M(T_{q_0})+d\rho_N(T_{q_0'})=T_{\theta_0}\Theta$, and the left side has dimension at most $\lvert M\rvert+\lvert N\rvert$. A point $\theta\in\mathrm{Im}M\cap\mathrm{Im}N$ has preimages $q,q'$, and $(q,q')$ lies in the fibre product. Testing a product in $\mathsf{Meth}$ against pointed two-point $0$-manifolds shows that its points are exactly the pairs $(q,q')$ over a common $\theta$. For $\mathrm{LoRA}_1\times\text{Frozen}$, suppose a product $P$ exists, with $\iota:P\to Q_{\mathrm{LoRA}_1}=\mathbb R^2$. The forgetful functor $\mathbf{Diff}_*\to\mathbf{Diff}$ is a right adjoint (its left adjoint is $X\mapsto X\sqcup\mathrm{pt}$), so $P$ is also the pullback in $\mathbf{Diff}$ and may be tested with unpointed curves. Let $p^*$ be the unique point of $P$ over $(0,0)$. The two axis curves $t\mapsto(t,0)$ and $t\mapsto(0,t)$ lie over $\theta_0$, so each lifts to a smooth curve in $P$ through $p^*$, and their velocities map under $d\iota_{p^*}$ to $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$. Hence $\operatorname{rank}d\iota_{p^*}=2$. Rank is lower semicontinuous and at most $2$, so it equals $2$ near $p^*$, and $\iota$ maps a neighbourhood of $p^*$ onto a set containing an open subset of $\mathbb R^2$. The cross contains none. The argument works for every pointing of $\mathrm{LoRA}_1$. Under the standard pointing $(0,a_0)$ with $a_0\neq0$, the base point is a smooth point of the cross and the obstruction sits at the origin.

(c) Functoriality is $\rho_N\circ h=\rho_M$. For the converse, choose (axiom of choice) for each $\theta\in\mathrm{Im}M$ a preimage $s(\theta)$ under $\rho_N$ with $s(\theta_0)=q_0'$, and put $h=s\circ\rho_M$. In the example the only candidate is the cube root, which is not differentiable at $0$. ∎
referee_notes: Both referees confirmed (a)-(c). One referee (major) found the PEFT reading overreaching: transversality can never hold for two PEFT methods (|M|+|N| < dim Theta), Prop I.8(b) and Thm II.7 are image-level meets rather than products, 'every method' holds only for weight-space methods, merge-as-canonical-map is definitional, and 'no smooth h with h^3=id' was misworded. Repaired: the sufficient condition is now an embedded-submanifold (clean or linear) fibre product; added that products can fail to exist (LoRA_1 x Frozen on 1x1) and that an existing product has the set-level fibre product as underlying set; the proof addresses pointedness; S_1 is presented as only a first-order obstruction (t^3 vs u^5); commentary restricted.
round2_notes: Round 2 (math minor, faithful minor): statement and proof hold. Fixed: the non-existence of LoRA_1 x Frozen is now argued by the rank argument at p*, the point over the origin, with unpointed test curves (the forgetful functor is a right adjoint), so it covers every pointing including (0,a_0); 'PEFT regime' replaced by |M|+|N| < dim Theta. Commentary: the interval claim is restricted to methods pointed at theta_0 (HF FourierFT, VB-LoRA, init=False, LoRA-XS and quantised bases carry defects); mergeability as definitional is restricted to exact arithmetic on a full-precision base; Im M ∩ Im N separated from the product; meets are taken in the poset of subsets. Prop I.8's commentary now places the singularity at the origin, not at the base point.
public_statement: Treat a weight-space PEFT method as a pointed smooth map $\rho:(Q,q_0)\to(\Theta,\theta_0)$ with $\rho(q_0)=\theta_0$. In this pointed slice category the frozen model is initial and full fine-tuning is terminal, and the unique map to full fine-tuning is $\rho$ itself, i.e. merging into full-precision weights. The product of two methods is their fibre product over weight space whenever that fibre product exists as a manifold, for example for affine methods such as the two one-sided LoRAs whose product is LoRA-XS. When the product exists its image is the intersection of the two images. Products can fail to exist ($\mathrm{LoRA}_1\times$ Frozen on $1\times1$ weights), and an inclusion of images gives only a set-level simulation, which need not be smooth ($t$ against $u^3$ on $\mathbb R$).

name: $S_1$ is functorial
statement: **Observation I.6 ($S_1$ is functorial).** [Obs] If $M\to N$ is a (pointed) morphism, then $S_1(M)\subseteq S_1(N)$. In particular, isomorphic methods have equal $S_1$ and equal first-order deficit. Monotonicity holds only along pointed morphisms: a weak morphism, such as a gauge map moving $q_0$ inside its fibre, can change $S_1$.
proof: *Proof.* Apply the chain rule $d\rho_N\circ dh=d\rho_M$ at $q_0$, using $h(q_0)=q_0'$. If $h$ is an isomorphism, $dh_q$ is invertible for every $q$, so $\operatorname{rank}d\rho_M(q)=\operatorname{rank}d\rho_N(h(q))$. Hence $d(M)=d(N)$ (equivalently $\mathrm{Im}\,M=\mathrm{Im}\,N$), and since $dh_{q_0}$ is surjective, $S_1(M)=S_1(N)$. So the deficits agree. ∎
referee_notes: Both referees: true as written. Wording fixes: the proof now shows d(M)=d(N) for isomorphisms (rank is invariant under a diffeomorphism); monotonicity is stated only along pointed morphisms. 'What this explains' rewritten: the lazy kernel depends on J_f and Lambda as well as S_1, Malladi et al. found random-A0 LoRA's kernel close to full fine-tuning's, and the image does distinguish split inits (it determines P).
round2_notes: Not covered by round 2; round-1 status kept.
public_statement: If one weight-space method simulates another by a pointed map, the first-order image of the first lies inside that of the second, so isomorphic methods have the same first-order image and the same first-order deficit. Monotonicity holds only along pointed maps; a gauge move of the starting point inside its fibre can change the first-order image.

name: additive monoidal structure
statement:
**Observation I.7 (additive monoidal structure).** [Obs] $\Theta$ is a vector space, so every object of $\mathsf{Meth}(\Theta,\theta_0)$ can be written $\rho=\theta_0+\delta$ with $\delta:=\rho-\theta_0$ and $\delta(q_0)=0$. Put
$$M\oplus N:=(Q_M\times Q_N,(q_0,q_0'),\theta_0+\delta_M+\delta_N).$$
This is a symmetric monoidal structure with the frozen model as unit. Its image is the Minkowski sum $\theta_0+(\mathrm{Im}\,\delta_M+\mathrm{Im}\,\delta_N)$. The operation $\oplus$ is not the categorical product, whose image, when the product exists, is $\cap$ (Obs I.4(b)). "Additive" in Def I.2 ($\delta$ independent of $\theta_0$) is a condition on *families* $\theta_0\mapsto M(\theta_0)$; it matters for base change (Exposé V), not here.

Write $\mathrm{LoRA}_k$ for LoRA with frozen residual $\theta_0$; for split pointings the sum below has residual $\theta_0-P-P'$. Concatenation $h(B_1,A_1,B_2,A_2)=([B_1\,B_2],[A_1;A_2])$ is an isomorphism $\mathrm{LoRA}_r\oplus\mathrm{LoRA}_s\cong\mathrm{LoRA}_{r+s}$ of unpointed objects. It is a pointed isomorphism onto $\mathrm{LoRA}_{r+s}$ pointed at $([B_0\,B_0'],[A_0;A_0'])$. For $\mathrm T_A$ pointings ($B_0=0$, $\operatorname{rank}A_0=r$), the target pointing has $\operatorname{rank}[A_0;A_0']=r+s$ iff $\mathrm{row}\,A_0\cap\mathrm{row}\,A_0'=0$; it lies in the stratum $\mathrm T_A$ of Thm II.2 when moreover $r+s<\min(m,n)$.

Standard pointings ($\mathrm T_A$, or symmetrically $\mathrm T_B$) exist only for $r<\min(m,n)$ (Thm II.2), so the monoidal question is pointwise. If $F(r)$ and $F(2r)$ are standard ($2r<\min(m,n)$), then $F(r)\oplus F(r)\not\cong F(2r)$ as pointed objects; for $2r\ge\min(m,n)$ no standard $F(2r)$ exists. Hence no assignment $r\mapsto\mathrm{LoRA}_r$ with $F(1)$ and $F(2)$ standard is **strong monoidal** into pointed objects. For $r\neq s$ and standard pointings, $F(r)\oplus F(s)\cong F(r+s)$ as pointed objects exactly when the row space of the target's $A_0$ is the direct sum of the two source row spaces. The assignment is strong monoidal on unpointed objects, up to weak morphisms, and on pointed objects with degenerate pointings: the origin $(B_0,A_0)=(0,0)$, where $S_1=0$, or the stacked pointings $F(r)=F(1)^{\oplus r}$. Concatenation is strictly associative and unital, so discrete $(\mathbb N,+)$ suffices for a plain strong monoidal functor. *Symmetric* strong monoidality needs the permutation groupoid, since swapping and then concatenating permutes the blocks.

With per-adapter scales $s_r$ ($\alpha/r$ for LoRA, $\alpha/\sqrt r$ for rsLoRA) and any target scale $s_*$, the map $h=([B_1\,B_2],[c_1A_1;c_2A_2])$ with $c_i=s_{r_i}/s_*$ is an isomorphism over $\Theta$. It is a linear bijection and preserves row spaces, so the pointing criterion is unchanged. HF PEFT's `add_weighted_adapter(..., combination_type="cat")` evaluates such a map at trained points: it sets `lora_alpha` to the new rank, so $s_*=1$, and multiplies each $A_i$ by $w_is_{r_i}$, so $c_i=w_is_{r_i}$. It is the isomorphism $h$ when all weights $w_i=1$ and the merged adapter has `use_rslora=False`. For rsLoRA sources, released PEFT versions through v0.21.1 copy `use_rslora=True` into the merged config and so overscale the merge by $\sqrt{r+s}$; PR #3449 on main fixes this.
proof: *Proof.* The coherence isomorphisms of $\oplus$ are those of the cartesian structure on $\mathbf{Diff}_*$. They lie over $\Theta$ because $+$ is associative and commutative, and the frozen model is a unit because its $\delta$ is $0$. Next, $[B_1\,B_2][A_1;A_2]=B_1A_1+B_2A_2$, and $h$ is a linear bijection. The pointing claim is $\dim(U+V)=r+s-\dim(U\cap V)$ for $U=\mathrm{row}A_0$, $V=\mathrm{row}A_0'$. For the negative claim, any pointed isomorphism preserves $S_1$ (Obs I.6). If $F(r)$ is standard, $S_1(F(r)\oplus F(r))=\{XA_0+X'A_0\}$ has dimension $mr$, while a standard $F(2r)$ has $\dim S_1=2mr$. For $r\neq s$, $S_1(F(r)\oplus F(s))=\{Y[A_0;A_0']\}$ equals $S_1(F(r+s))=\{XA_0''\}$ iff $\mathrm{row}A_0''=\mathrm{row}A_0\oplus\mathrm{row}A_0'$; then concatenation followed by the gauge $g\in GL_{r+s}$ with $g[A_0;A_0']=A_0''$ is a pointed isomorphism. The degenerate cases are direct. ∎ [Num: at $m=7$, $\dim S_1=28$ for a standard $\mathrm{LoRA}_4$, against $14$ for $\mathrm{LoRA}_2\oplus\mathrm{LoRA}_2$ with the same $A_0$ and $28$ with independent $A_0$'s; $F(1)\oplus F(2)$ and a standard $F(3)$ both give $21$.]
referee_notes: Refuted as written: 'strong monoidal only on unpointed objects' is false (the origin pointing and stacked pointings give pointed strong monoidal functors), and the claim was unproved for standard pointings. Repaired: no choice of standard pointings makes r -> LoRA_r strong monoidal, proved via S_1 dimensions (mr vs 2mr); (+) defined on all of Meth via the vector-space structure ('additive' is a condition on families); residuals and HF's alpha/r scaling handled; symmetric only over the permutation groupoid; the product's image is the intersection only when it exists. Commentary corrected: UniPELT and MAM are not (+)-words, and LoRA-soup CAT is a span of frozen line methods.
round2_notes: Round 2 (math refuted on a PEFT sentence, minor; faithful refuted, major): the HF claim was false. HF's add_weighted_adapter(cat) sets the merged scale to 1 (lora_alpha = new rank) with c_i = w_i s_{r_i}, and released PEFT through v0.21.1 copies use_rslora=True, overscaling rsLoRA merges by sqrt(r+s) (fixed on main by PR #3449). Repaired: the isomorphism is stated for any target scale s_*, and HF's cat is described exactly. The negative monoidal claim is now pointwise (standard pointings exist only for r < min(m,n); threshold 2r >= min(m,n)), the r != s case is characterised by a direct-sum row-space condition, and plain strong monoidality from discrete (N,+) is separated from symmetric monoidality. Proof gains the coherence line. Commentary: the sum of k LoRAs is isomorphic (not equal) to LoRA_{kr}, with different training dynamics under alpha/r scaling; HF cat is h at trained points; CAT soups give a span of dimension at most k; ReLoRA ignores its warm start. Prop V.4's cat bullet made consistent.
public_statement: Because weight space is a vector space, adding the updates of two weight-space methods on the product of their parameter spaces makes pointed methods a symmetric monoidal category, with the frozen model as unit and the Minkowski sum of updates as image. This sum is not the categorical product, whose image, when it exists, is the intersection. Block concatenation, with the $A$-blocks rescaled to match $\alpha/r$-type scales, identifies $\mathrm{LoRA}_r\oplus\mathrm{LoRA}_s$ with $\mathrm{LoRA}_{r+s}$ over weight space, and as pointed methods exactly at the concatenated initialisation. For zero-$B$ initialisations the result is again a standard one iff $\mathrm{row}A_0\cap\mathrm{row}A_0'=0$ and $r+s<\min(m,n)$. No choice of standard initialisations makes $\mathrm{LoRA}_r\oplus\mathrm{LoRA}_r$ isomorphic to $\mathrm{LoRA}_{2r}$, since the first-order image has dimension $mr$ against $2mr$. HF PEFT's `cat` merge applies this map at trained points with merged scale $1$.

name: a product that produces a named method; an image-level meet
statement:
**Proposition I.8 (a product that produces a named method; an image-level meet).** [Prop]

(a) Let $A_0\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}$ have full row rank and $B_0\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}$ full column rank. Define the one-sided methods
$$\mathrm{FA}(A_0):B\mapsto W_0+BA_0,\qquad\mathrm{FB}(B_0):A\mapsto W_0+B_0A,$$
both pointed at $0$. Then
$$\mathrm{FA}(A_0)\times\mathrm{FB}(B_0)\;\cong\;(\mathbb R^{r\times r},0,\ R\mapsto W_0+B_0RA_0).$$
The product supplies this sandwich for *any* frames. Assume $\operatorname{rank}W_0\ge r$ ($\sigma_r>0$) and take the SVD frames $B_0=U_r$, $A_0=\Sigma_rV_r^\top$: the result is **LoRA-XS pointed at $R=0$**. The LoRA-XS paper writes $xW+xARB$ in row-vector convention with $A=U_r\Sigma_r$ and $B=V_r^\top$; transposed, the update is $B_0R^\top A_0$, so the isomorphism is $R\mapsto\alpha R^\top$. LoRA-XS initialises $R\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)$ with $\sigma=10^{-5}$, a negligible pointing defect.

(b) Let $W_0$ have full row rank (so $m\le n$), and let $\mathrm{LoRA}_r$ carry its standard pointing ($B_0=0$, image $W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}$). The image-level meet of $\mathrm{LoRA}_r$ with the output-scaling method $\ell\mapsto\mathrm{diag}(\ell)W_0$ is $\{\mathrm{diag}(\ell)W_0:\#\{i:\ell_i\neq1\}\le r\}$, that is, "rescale at most $r$ output neurons". The output-scaling method is the key/value part of (IA)$^3$. On the FFN, (IA)$^3$ scales the *input* of $W_{\rm down}$, $W\mapsto W\mathrm{diag}(\ell)$; the mirror statement then needs full column rank, or holds generically for $r<d$.
proof:
*Proof.* (a) A point of the fibre product is a pair $(B,A)$ with $BA_0=B_0A=:D$. Then $\mathrm{row}\,D\subseteq\mathrm{row}\,A_0$ and $\mathrm{col}\,D\subseteq\mathrm{col}\,B_0$, so $D=B_0RA_0$ for a unique $R$. Since $A_0$ has full row rank, $BA_0=B_0RA_0$ forces $B=B_0R$, and likewise $A=RA_0$. So the fibre product is the $r^2$-dimensional linear subspace $\{(B_0R,RA_0)\}$, and $R\mapsto(B_0R,RA_0)$ is a smooth bijection onto it with smooth inverse $(B,A)\mapsto B_0^+B$. Any pair of maps $(h_1,h_2):T\to Q_{\rm FA}\times Q_{\rm FB}$ that agree over $\Theta$ factors through it via $t\mapsto B_0^+h_1(t)$, so this is the product in $\mathbf{Diff}$. If $\operatorname{rank}W_0<r$, then $\Sigma_rV_r^\top$ is rank-deficient and the LoRA-XS instance breaks.

(b) $\mathrm{diag}(\ell)W_0-W_0=\mathrm{diag}(\ell-\mathbf 1)W_0$, and its rank is $\#\{i:\ell_i\ne1\}$ because the rows of $W_0$ are independent. ∎ [Num: the fibre product of (a) has dimension $4=r^2$ at $(m,n,r)=(6,8,2)$.]
referee_notes: Both referees: correct. Wording fixes: rank W0 >= r is needed for the LoRA-XS instance; LoRA-XS initialises R ~ N(0, 1e-10), a negligible defect now in the approximate-pointing footnote, and its row-vector convention gives the isomorphism R -> alpha R^T; LoRA carries its standard pointing in (b); (IA)^3 is an output scaling only on k and v (input-side on W_down). The gloss that LoRA_r x (IA)^3 is a new sparse-rescaling method was withdrawn: the meet is set-level only (the fibre product is singular), and with a fixed support it is masked (IA)^3 (cf. Stoehr et al. 2024).
round2_notes: Not covered by round 2; round-1 status kept. Round-2 knock-on (from I.4's faithful review): the commentary now places the singularity of the (b) fibre product at the origin, not at the base point, and describes its components.
public_statement: Freezing the frame on either side of LoRA gives two one-sided methods, $B\mapsto W_0+BA_0$ and $A\mapsto W_0+B_0A$. Their categorical product is the sandwich $R\mapsto W_0+B_0RA_0$, and with the SVD frames of $W_0$ it is exactly LoRA-XS. By contrast, what LoRA$_r$ and the output-scaling part of (IA)$^3$ can both reach is the set of weights that rescale at most $r$ output neurons; this is an intersection of images only, and the two methods have no product.

name: pointings of an additive method
statement:
**Theorem II.1 (pointings of an additive method).** [Thm; elementary. The rank-$2r$ consequence is known in practice as the PiSSA$\to$LoRA conversion (Meng et al. 2024), implemented in HF PEFT] Let $M=(Q,q_0,\theta_0+\delta)$ be additive with shape $C=\delta(Q)$. Write $-v+C$ for a translate, and $C-C:=\{c-c':c,c'\in C\}$ for the Minkowski difference.

(a) For each $q\in Q$, the re-pointed method $M_q:=(Q,q,\theta_0-\delta(q)+\delta(\cdot))$, with frozen residual $\theta_0-\delta(q)$, is pointed at $\theta_0$, and $\mathrm{Im}\,M_q=\theta_0+(-\delta(q)+C)$.

(b) $\bigcup_q\mathrm{Im}\,M_q=\theta_0+(C-C)$.

(c) For LoRA$_r$ on a single linear box with $s\ne0$, $C-C=\mathcal M_{\le\min(2r,m,n)}$; for several boxes, $C-C$ is the product of the per-box varieties $\mathcal M_{\le\min(2r,m_i,n_i)}$. Hence **no exact pointing of LoRA$_r$ (frozen residual $\theta_0-\delta(q)$), whether zero-init or split (PiSSA, OLoRA, CorDA, LoRA-GA), makes an update $\theta-\theta_0$ of rank $>2r$ reachable in any adapted matrix.** More robustly, from *any* starting point $q_0$ of LoRA$_r$, pointed or not, $\rho(q)-\rho(q_0)=\delta(q)-\delta(q_0)$ has rank $\le\min(2r,m,n)$. Quantised-residual schemes (QLoRA, LoftQ, QPiSSA) are pointed only up to an order-dependent defect ($e$ for QLoRA; see Prop V.2(b) for the others); measured from $\theta_0$ rather than from their starting weight, their updates contain a generically full-rank part of the quantisation error. The bound $2r$ is attained by split pointings when $2r\le\min(m,n)$.
proof: *Proof.* (a) and (b) are immediate from the definitions. (c) $\operatorname{rank}(X-Y)\le 2r$. Conversely, $C$ is a cone and so closed under negation; split the SVD of a rank-$\le 2r$ matrix as $Z=Z_1+Z_2$ with $\operatorname{rank}Z_i\le r$, and write $Z=Z_1-(-Z_2)$. ∎
referee_notes: Both referees: correct. Wording fixes: the method, not delta, is additive; translate and Minkowski difference distinguished; single box with s != 0 in (c), per-box products for several boxes. The bold conclusion now concerns exact pointings and adds the robust form (rank <= 2r measured from any starting point); quantised-residual schemes fall outside it when measured from theta0. Attributed to the PiSSA-to-LoRA conversion of Meng et al. 2024; split inits lose generic updates of every rank >= 1.
round2_notes: Not covered by round 2; round-1 status kept. Round-2 knock-on (from V.2): the sentence on quantised-residual schemes now cites their order-dependent defects instead of a single defect e.
public_statement: For an additive method, moving the starting point while subtracting a frozen residual keeps the method pointed at the pretrained weights, and the union of all such re-pointed images is $\theta_0$ plus the difference set $C-C$ of its update shape. For LoRA$_r$ that difference set is the matrices of rank at most $\min(2r,m,n)$, so no exact initialisation of LoRA$_r$, zero-init or split (PiSSA, OLoRA, CorDA, LoRA-GA), makes an update of rank above $2r$ reachable in any adapted matrix. Split initialisations attain $2r$ when $2r\le\min(m,n)$.

name: three strata of LoRA initialisations
statement:
**Theorem II.2 (three strata of LoRA initialisations).** [Thm] Let $\delta(B,A)=BA$ with $1\le r<\min(m,n)$. Consider pointed LoRA objects in three distinguished strata of full-rank pointings (pointings whose nonzero factors have full rank). Only $\mathrm S$ is open and dense in the space of pointings; $\mathrm T_A$ and $\mathrm T_B$ are nowhere dense.
- $(\mathrm T_A)$: $B_0=0$ and $\operatorname{rank}A_0=r$;
- $(\mathrm T_B)$: $A_0=0$ and $\operatorname{rank}B_0=r$;
- $(\mathrm S)$: $\operatorname{rank}B_0A_0=r$, with frozen residual $\theta_0-B_0A_0$.

(a) **Classification.** Within a stratum, $M_{q_0}\cong M_{q_0'}$ iff, respectively, $\mathrm{row}\,A_0=\mathrm{row}\,A_0'$; $\mathrm{col}\,B_0=\mathrm{col}\,B_0'$; or $B_0A_0=B_0'A_0'$. Objects in different strata are never isomorphic. As a *set*, the isomorphism classes of the three strata therefore form
$$\mathrm{Gr}(r,\mathbb R^n)\ \sqcup\ \mathrm{Gr}(r,\mathbb R^m)\ \sqcup\ \mathcal M_r(m\times n).$$
(b) **First order.** $\dim S_1$ is $mr$, $nr$ and $r(m+n-r)$ respectively, while $d=r(m+n-r)$ in every case. The deficits are $r(n-r)$, $r(m-r)$ and $0$.

(c) **Geometry.** In $\mathrm T_A$ and $\mathrm T_B$, $\mathrm{Im}=\theta_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}$, whose vertex $\theta_0$ is an **apex**. In $\mathrm S$, $\mathrm{Im}=(\theta_0-P)+\mathcal M_{\le r}$ with $P=B_0A_0$, and $\theta_0$ is a **smooth point**.

(d) **Incomparability.** The images of $\mathrm S$-type and $\mathrm T$-type objects are incomparable.

(e) **Scope.** The three strata do not exhaust the pointings of LoRA$_r$. Outside them lie: $B_0=0$ with $\operatorname{rank}A_0<r$; $A_0=0$ with $\operatorname{rank}B_0<r$; $B_0=A_0=0$; $0<\operatorname{rank}B_0A_0<r$; and pointings with $B_0,A_0$ both nonzero and $B_0A_0=0$. HF PEFT ships one of the last kind: `init_lora_weights="orthogonal"` (which requires $r$ even) lies in the stratum $(\operatorname{rk}B_0,\operatorname{rk}A_0,\operatorname{rk}B_0A_0)=(r/2,r/2,0)$, an apex with $\dim S_1=\tfrac r2(m+n-\tfrac r2)$. It is isomorphic to no object of the three strata. Its image $\theta_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}$ rules out $\mathrm S$, and its $S_1$ determines $(\mathrm{col}\,B_0,\mathrm{row}\,A_0)$, of dimensions $(r/2,r/2)$, against $(0,r)$ in $\mathrm T_A$ and $(r,0)$ in $\mathrm T_B$. The dimension of $S_1$ alone does not separate it, since at $(m,n,r)=(4,5,2)$ it equals $mr$. This placement holds in exact arithmetic; HF casts the two factors to the base dtype separately, and in bf16 the result is a generic pointing with a tiny defect. For every pointing, the image determines $P=B_0A_0$ (its vertex is $\theta_0-P$), and $S_1=\{XA_0+B_0Y\}$ determines $(\mathrm{row}\,A_0,\mathrm{col}\,B_0)$ whenever these are proper subspaces. The classification is set-level: in the space of pointings $\mathrm T_A$ lies in the closure of $\mathrm S$, since $(\varepsilon B',A_0)\to(0,A_0)$, so the quotient is not a topological disjoint union.
proof:
*Proof.*
- *"If" in (a).* Two full-row-rank matrices with the same row space satisfy $A_0'=gA_0$ for a unique $g\in GL_r$, and $(B,A)\mapsto(Bg^{-1},gA)$ is a pointed isomorphism over $\Theta$. $\mathrm T_B$ is symmetric. In $\mathrm S$, the full-rank factorisations of $P$ form one $GL_r$-orbit, and the residuals agree.
- *"Only if" in (a).* In $\mathrm T_A$, $d\rho_{(0,A_0)}(\dot B,\dot A)=\dot BA_0$. So $S_1=\{XA_0\}$ is the set of matrices whose row space lies in $\mathrm{row}A_0$; it determines $\mathrm{row}A_0$, and it is an isomorphism invariant by Obs I.6. $\mathrm T_B$ is symmetric. In $\mathrm S$, the image $(\theta_0-P)+\mathcal M_{\le r}$ is an isomorphism invariant and determines its vertex: $\mathrm{Sing}\,\mathcal M_{\le s}=\mathcal M_{\le s-1}$ for $1\le s\le r<\min(m,n)$, algebraically and in the $C^1$ sense (a non-linear cone is not $C^1$ at its vertex), so iterating the singular locus $r$ times leaves the single point $\theta_0-P$. Hence the image determines $P$. A shorter route avoids singular loci: if $c+\mathcal M_{\le r}=c'+\mathcal M_{\le r}$ with $D=c-c'\neq0$, a generic $X$ of rank $r$ gives $\operatorname{rank}(D+X)=\min(\operatorname{rk}D+r,m,n)\ge r+1$, so $c+X\notin c'+\mathcal M_{\le r}$.
- *Separating the strata.* $S_1(\mathrm T_A)=\{Z:\mathrm{row}Z\subseteq V\}$ contains $e_iv^\top$ for every $i$ and every $v\in V$, so it equals $S_1(\mathrm T_B)=\{Z:\mathrm{col}Z\subseteq U\}$ only if $U=\mathbb R^m$, which is impossible since $r<m$. (When $m\ne n$ the dimensions $mr\ne nr$ already differ.) $\mathrm S$ differs from both because $\dim S_1=r(m+n-r)$ differs from $mr$ (as $n>r$) and from $nr$ (as $m>r$).
- *(b).* At a full-rank pair, $S_1=\{XA_0+B_0Y\}=T_P\mathcal M_r$. In general $\dim\{XA_0+B_0Y\}=m\operatorname{rk}A_0+n\operatorname{rk}B_0-\operatorname{rk}A_0\operatorname{rk}B_0$ (Prop II.3).
- *(c).* $\mathcal M_r$ is open in $\mathcal M_{\le r}$ and is a manifold of dimension $r(m+n-r)$, so $P$, of rank $r$, is a smooth point, and $\theta_0$ is a smooth point of the $\mathrm S$-image. In the $\mathrm T$ strata, $\theta_0$ is the vertex of the non-linear cone $\theta_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}$, a singular point (Def I.5), and by (b) its deficit is positive, so it is an apex.
- *(d).* A generic rank-one $X$ satisfies $\operatorname{rank}(P+X)=\operatorname{rank}(X-P)=r+1$. So $\theta_0+X$ lies in the $\mathrm T$-image but not in the $\mathrm S$-image, and $\theta_0-P+X$ lies in the $\mathrm S$-image but not in the $\mathrm T$-image.
- *(e).* The dimension is Prop II.3. For every pointing, $S_1=\{XA_0+B_0Y\}=\{Z:Z(\mathrm{row}\,A_0)^\perp\subseteq\mathrm{col}\,B_0\}$, whose Frobenius annihilator is $(\mathrm{col}\,B_0)^\perp\otimes(\mathrm{row}\,A_0)^\perp$. When both subspaces are proper, the column and row spans of this annihilator recover them, so $S_1$ determines the pair and its dimensions, and by Obs I.6 so does every pointed isomorphism class. The image determines its vertex $\theta_0-P$ by the translation argument above. HF's `orthogonal` init draws one orthogonal $Q\in O(r)$ and sets $A_0=(G_AQ_{[0::2]})^\top/10$, $B_0=G_BQ_{[1::2]}/10$, from the even- and odd-indexed rows of $Q$, so $B_0A_0=0$ with both factors of rank $r/2$. ∎ [Num: $\dim S_1=(14,10,20)$ for $(\mathrm T_A,\mathrm T_B,\mathrm S)$ at $(m,n,r)=(7,5,2)$, and $11$ for HF's `orthogonal` init.]

Fixed: 'generic (full-rank)' is now 'full-rank', with S open dense and T_A, T_B nowhere dense (also in Exposé 0); HF orthogonal init is separated from the strata by the S_1 subspace (annihilator (col B0)^perp ⊗ (row A0)^perp), since dim S_1 alone coincides with mr at (4,5,2); r even and exact-arithmetic caveats added; the S 'only if' gains the translation argument. public_statement: For LoRA of rank $r<\min(m,n)$ on one $m\times n$ weight, take three strata of exact full-rank initialisations: $B_0=0$ with full-rank $A_0$ (vanilla LoRA on linear layers, EVA), $A_0=0$ with full-rank $B_0$ (Init[B], HF's default on embedding layers), and a rank-$r$ $B_0A_0$ subtracted from the frozen weight (PiSSA, MiLoRA, OLoRA, CorDA, LoRA-GA, Astra). Two pointed LoRA methods in these strata are isomorphic over weight space exactly when they share $\mathrm{row}\,A_0$, $\mathrm{col}\,B_0$ or $B_0A_0$ respectively, so as a set the classes are $\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)\sqcup\mathrm{Gr}(r,m)\sqcup\mathcal M_r$. Zero-factor initialisations sit at the apex of the cone $W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}$ with $r(n-r)$ or $r(m-r)$ fewer first-order directions; split initialisations sit at a smooth point, and neither image contains the other. The result is set-level and in exact arithmetic, concerns expressivity and first-order reach, and excludes rank-deficient pointings such as HF's `orthogonal` init, frozen-factor sub-objects (LoRA-FA, MiCA) and quantised-base defects (QLoRA, LoftQ).

name: first-order rank formula: smoothness, alignment and scale
statement:
**Proposition II.3 (first-order rank formula: smoothness, alignment and scale).** [Prop] For $\kappa(B,A)=W_{\rm base}+sBA$ with $s\ne0$,
$$\operatorname{rank}d\kappa_{(B,A)}=m\operatorname{rk}A+n\operatorname{rk}B-\operatorname{rk}A\operatorname{rk}B\qquad\text{for all }(B,A),$$
and $\{XA\}\cap\{BY\}=\{BRA:R\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\}$. For full-rank frames this overlap is the tangent space of the product $\mathrm{FA}(A)\times\mathrm{FB}(B)$ of Prop I.8(a), re-based at $\kappa(B,A)$, whose image is the meet of the two one-sided images: a generalised LoRA-XS. It is LoRA-XS proper when $(B,A)$ span the top-$r$ singular subspaces of $W_0$ ($\sigma_r>0$), as at a PiSSA init; bottom frames (MiLoRA) give a generalised LoRA-XS.

Under gradient flow $\dot B=-\eta_B\nabla_BL$, $\dot A=-\eta_A\nabla_AL$, with $G=\nabla_WL$,
$$\tfrac{d}{dt}L=-s^2\big(\eta_B\|GA^\top\|_F^2+\eta_A\|B^\top G\|_F^2\big)$$
at every time, in particular at $(B_0,A_0)$. To first order in the step sizes the same holds for full-batch gradient descent, and in expectation for unbiased minibatch SGD. Under Adam ($\varepsilon\to0$, with bias correction) the first step changes the loss by $-\lvert s\rvert\big(\eta_B\|GA_0^\top\|_1+\eta_A\|B_0^\top G\|_1\big)+O(\eta^2)$, with entrywise $\ell_1$ norms. This first-order term is linear in $\lvert s\rvert$, against quadratic under gradient flow.
proof: *Proof.* The image of $d\kappa$ is $\{XA\}+\{BY\}$, whose summands are the matrices with row space in $\mathrm{row}A$ (dimension $m\operatorname{rk}A$) and with column space in $\mathrm{col}B$ (dimension $n\operatorname{rk}B$). A matrix $D$ lies in both iff $D\in\mathrm{col}B\otimes\mathrm{row}A$, of dimension $\operatorname{rk}A\operatorname{rk}B$, and then $D=B(B^+DA^+)A$. The gradient-flow rate is $\langle G,\dot W\rangle$ with $\dot W=-s^2(\eta_BGA^\top A+\eta_ABB^\top G)$. Adam's first step is $\delta B=-\eta_B\,\mathrm{sign}(sGA^\top)$, so $\langle G,s\,\delta B\,A\rangle=-\lvert s\rvert\eta_B\|GA^\top\|_1$, and likewise for $A$. ∎ [Num: the rank formula holds in 400 random cases including rank-deficient factors; the rate matches finite differences.]
referee_notes: Rank formula and overlap identity confirmed for all (B,A). Defects: kappa lacked the scale s although the rate carries s^2; the rate needs a gradient-flow hypothesis (Adam's first step gives an entrywise l1 rate, linear in s); 'LoRA-XS in the frames' is a generalised LoRA-XS. Commentary errors: EVA does not maximise ||G A0^T|| (it is a data-only proxy valid under its own assumptions; LoRA-GA's gradient SVD gives the maximising A_0 (its B_0 is not the maximiser; see round 2)), and factor scale is a third, confounding mechanism. All repaired in the statement and the commentary.
round2_notes: Round 2 (math minor, faithful minor): statement and proof hold. Fixed: the overlap is the tangent space of the product FA x FB (whose image is the meet); LoRA-XS proper needs top-r frames; SGD holds to first order for full-batch GD and in expectation for minibatches; Adam rate written with |s| and as a first-order term. Commentary: LoRA-GA aligns only A_0 (its B_0 = U_{r+1:2r} gives up rate to approximate the rank-2r truncation of G); HF's scale='stable' scales only B; EVA's Thm 3.2 assumptions and HF's centred PCA stated correctly; alignment is a gradient-flow/SGD notion; 'leave the apex' corrected to 'start off the apex'. The round-1 note that LoRA-GA's gradient SVD is the maximiser holds for A_0 only.
public_statement: For LoRA's map $W_{\rm base}+sBA$ with $s\ne0$, the differential has rank $m\,\mathrm{rk}A+n\,\mathrm{rk}B-\mathrm{rk}A\,\mathrm{rk}B$ at every point. The $A$-moves and $B$-moves overlap exactly in $\{BRA\}$, so zero-factor initialisations (LoRA, QLoRA, EVA, LoRA-FA) start with $mr$ first-order directions and full-rank split initialisations (PiSSA, OLoRA, CorDA, LoRA-GA) with $r(m+n-r)$; at a PiSSA init the overlap is LoRA-XS's update space. Under gradient flow the loss falls at rate $s^2(\eta_B\|GA^\top\|_F^2+\eta_A\|B^\top G\|_F^2)$. Among orthonormal $A_0$ at zero init, the top right singular space of $G$ maximises this, and that is LoRA-GA's $A_0$ (not its $B_0$). Adam's first step ($\varepsilon\to0$) lowers the loss, to first order in the step size, by $\lvert s\rvert(\eta_B\|GA_0^\top\|_1+\eta_A\|B_0^\top G\|_1)$, which is linear in $\lvert s\rvert$ and depends on the basis of $A_0$.

name: zero gate
statement:
**Lemma II.4 (zero gate).** [Lemma] Let $Q=U\times V$ with $U$ a vector space, let $\rho=\theta_0+\beta(u,v)$ with $\beta$ smooth, and suppose $\beta(u_0,v)=0$ for all $v$; for example $\beta(\cdot,v)$ linear and $u_0=0$. Then $D_v\rho_{q_0}=0$. Hence $\nabla_v(L\circ\rho)(q_0)=0$, $S_1=D_u\beta(u_0,v_0)(U)$ ($=\beta(U,v_0)$ in the linear case), and the cometric at $q_0$ is $K_{q_0}=D_u\beta\,\Lambda_{uu}\,D_u\beta^\top$, where $\Lambda_{uu}$ is the $uu$-block of $\Lambda$; no block-diagonality is needed, since the $v$-columns of $D\rho$ vanish. The weight trajectory $\theta(t)$ agrees with that of the method with $v$ frozen at $v_0$ to first order in $t$ (gradient flow), or in the step size (one or more Adam steps). The parameter $v$ itself may still move: under terms not of the form $L\circ\rho$ (regularisers, decoupled weight decay), and under Adam, whose step-2 move of $v$ is $O(\eta)$ although its effect on $\theta$ is $O(\eta^2)$.

*Function-level variant.* For an extension with realised function $F(u,v,x)$, if $F(u_0,v,x)=F_0(x)$ for all $v$ and $x$, then $D_vF=0$ at $q_0$, with the same conclusions at the level of functions. No linearity is needed.
proof: *Proof.* $\beta(u_0,v)=0$ for all $v$, so $D_v\beta(u_0,v_0)=0$. The rest follows from the chain rule. The function-level variant is identical. ∎ [Num: under Adam with $\eta\in\{10^{-2},10^{-3},10^{-4}\}$, the step-2 move of $A$ in zero-init LoRA scales as $\eta$, while the deviation of $\Delta W$ from the frozen-$A$ method scales as $\eta^2$.]
referee_notes: Both referees: lemma correct. Wording repaired: hypotheses stated explicitly and weakened to beta(u0,v)=0; K uses the uu-block of Lambda; 'frozen' stated for the weight trajectory to first order (v itself may move under regularisers, weight decay, or Adam at step 2); a function-level variant added for LLaMA-Adapter and zero-up-projection adapters. Instance corrections: AdaLoRA's orthogonality penalty moves P and Q at step one; dim S_1 = r only for generic P, Q; LoRA and LoRA-FA agree at first order only for LoRA-FA's original plain-gradient form.
round2_notes: Not covered by round 2; round-1 status kept.
public_statement: If a method's update vanishes identically while one block of parameters sits at its initial value, as LoRA's does at $B=0$, then the other block receives zero gradient at initialisation, the first-order image and the initial cometric come from the first block alone, and the weight trajectory agrees to first order with the method that freezes the other block (under gradient flow, or Adam to first order in the step size). Examples are LoRA at $B=0$, VeRA, AdaLoRA at $\Lambda=0$, LLaMA-Adapter's zero gate, and adapters with a zero up-projection.

name: complete invariants of the basic actions
statement:
**Theorem II.5 (complete invariants of the basic actions).** [Thm; classical] Let $W,W'\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$.
1. *Right orthogonal (input side).* $W'=WR$ for some $R\in O(n)$ iff $WW^\top=W'W'^\top$. For $SO(n)$, when $\operatorname{rank}W=n$, also require that the then unique $R$ have $\det R=1$.
2. *Left orthogonal.* $W'=PW$ for some $P\in O(m)$ iff $W^\top W=W'^\top W'$.
3. *Two-sided.* $W'=PWR$ for some $P\in O(m)$ and $R\in O(n)$ iff $W$ and $W'$ have the same singular values, counted with multiplicity.
4. *Left torus.* If $W$ has no zero row, $W'=DW$ for some $D\in T_m^+$ iff $w_i'\in\mathbb R_{>0}w_i$ for every $i$. For the full torus $T_m$, whose signs are unconstrained, the complete invariant is the set of zero rows together with the row *lines*.
5. *Full Hadamard torus.* $W'=E\odot W$ for some $E\in(\mathbb R^\times)^{m\times n}$ iff $W$ and $W'$ have the same zero pattern.
proof: *Proof.* (1) If all inner products of rows agree, the map $\sum c_iw_i\mapsto\sum c_iw_i'$ is well defined and isometric on the row spans, because $\|\sum c_iw_i\|^2=c^\top WW^\top c$. The two row spans have the same dimension, $\operatorname{rank}WW^\top$. Extend the map by an isometry of the orthogonal complements to $R^\top\in O(n)$; then $W'=WR$. The converse is immediate. (2) is (1) applied to transposes. (3) follows from the SVD. (4) and (5) hold entry by entry; for (5) put $E_{ij}=W'_{ij}/W_{ij}$ on the support and $1$ off it. ∎
referee_notes: Both referees: all five items true and classical. Wording fixes: quantifiers P in O(m), R in O(n) and multiplicity in (3); T_m^+ defined in the Conventions; (4) stated for rays, and for the full torus T_m (row lines plus zero rows); the full Hadamard torus distinguished from LoHa's two-sided diagonal torus; orientation condition for SO(n) when rank W = n; the first-fundamental-theorem remark made precise. Added the caveat that real methods ((IA)^3, DoRA, HiRA) can create zeros, so only 'zeros of W0 stay zero' transfers.
round2_notes: Not covered by round 2; round-1 status kept.
public_statement: Classical complete invariants decide when two weights differ by a basic action. They are related by an input-side orthogonal map iff they have the same neuron Gram matrix $WW^\top$, by an output-side one iff they have the same $W^\top W$, by orthogonal maps on both sides iff they have the same singular values, by a positive output scaling (for weights without zero rows) iff corresponding rows are positive multiples of each other, and by an entrywise nonzero Hadamard factor iff they have the same zero pattern.

name: what exactly orthogonal methods can never do
proof: *Proof.* Use Thm II.5(1) and (3), and the fact that a product of orthogonal factors is orthogonal. $(WR)_{:,J}=W_{:,J}R_J$ for block-diagonal $R$. For BOFT, $K_{\rm out}(W)_{ij}=s_is_jK_{\rm out}(W_0)_{ij}$, so $\cos'_{ij}=\mathrm{sign}(s_is_j)\cos_{ij}$ when $s_is_j\ne0$. For GOFT with its scaler, $W_0\mathrm{diag}(g)GG^\top\mathrm{diag}(g)W_0^\top=W_0\mathrm{diag}(g)^2W_0^\top$. For the Cayley–Neumann map, $(I-Q)(I+Q+Q^2+Q^3)=I-Q^4$, $C(Q)$ is orthogonal and commutes with $Q^4$, and $Q^4$ is symmetric with eigenvalues $\theta_k^4$ for skew $Q$. ∎ [Num: with $s=(-0.5,1,\dots,1)$, BOFT changes a cosine by $1.5$ while $\lvert\cos\rvert$ is fixed to $4\times10^{-16}$, and an all-negative $s$ fixes every cosine to $10^{-15}$; GOFT with a scaler $g=1\pm0.05$ moves cosines and singular values; a conformal block $\sqrt2\,\mathrm{Rot}(0.3)$ on two of $8$ input coordinates changes a cosine; HF's default OFT satisfies $R^\top R=(I-Q^4)^2$ to $5\times10^{-16}$, with $\lVert R^\top R-I\rVert=1.5\times10^{-2}$ already for block size $8$ and skew entries of size about $0.07$, and is singular at $\theta=1$.]

(2) 'Covers OFT' was false for HF PEFT's default Cayley-Neumann OFT, where R = C(Q)(I - Q^4) and R^T R = (I - Q^4)^2 != I, so K_out and the spectrum drift across merges; HF <= 0.13 and LyCORIS OFT act on the output side. GOFT's official code adds a trainable input scaler by default (no_scaling=False), so only strict GOFT is covered. public_statement: If every weight a method produces, including after merge-and-restart cycles, has the form $W_0R$ with $R$ exactly orthogonal on the input side, then in exact arithmetic the neuron Gram matrix $WW^\top$ never changes. So every neuron norm, every angle between neurons (and with them the hyperspherical energy) and every singular value of $W_0$ stay fixed, and block OFT with a fixed partition also fixes each block Gram. This covers exact-Cayley OFT and block OFT, strict GOFT without its optional scaler, HRA, and ETHER as defined in its paper. It does not cover variants with a per-neuron or per-input scale (HF BOFT, HF OFT 0.14 to 0.15, GOFT's default code), output-side variants, or approximately orthogonal ones such as HF PEFT's default Cayley-Neumann OFT, qGOFT and ETHER+.

name: HRA is the meet of LoRA with the rotation orbit, and it starts at an apex
statement:
**Theorem II.7 (HRA is the meet of LoRA with the rotation orbit, and it starts at an apex).** [Thm] Let $W_0\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ be injective ($\operatorname{rank}W_0=n$), and let $r$ be even with $2\le r\le n-2$. Define $\mathrm{HRA}_r:(u_1,\dots,u_r)\mapsto W_0H_{u_1}\cdots H_{u_r}$ with $u_i\ne0$, where $H_u=I-2uu^\top/\|u\|^2$. Write $\mathrm{OFT}_{SO}:=W_0\cdot SO(n)$ for the rotation orbit. (The $O(n)$-orbit would add the odd component: $W_0H_{e_1}$ lies in $W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}$ but not in $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{HRA}_r$.)

(a) **Meet.** $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{HRA}_r=(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r})\cap W_0\cdot SO(n)$. Further, $d(\mathrm{HRA}_r)=rn-\tfrac{r(r+1)}2$, so the generic fibre has dimension $\tfrac{r(r+1)}2=rn-d$. This gauge is non-linear. The evident continuous global symmetries are the $r$ scalings $u_i\mapsto c_iu_i$; the braid group also acts globally by Hurwitz moves $(u_i,u_{i+1})\mapsto(H_{u_i}u_{i+1},u_i)$, since $H_aH_b=H_{H_ab}H_a$.

(b) **First-order collapse.** At the paired initialisation $u_{2i-1}=u_{2i}=w_i$ ($i\le k=r/2$, with the $w_i$ independent and $U=\mathrm{span}\{w_i\}$),
$$S_1=W_0\cdot\{\Omega\in\mathfrak{so}(n):P_{U^\perp}\Omega P_{U^\perp}=0\},\qquad\dim S_1=kn-\tfrac{k(k+1)}2<d(\mathrm{HRA}_r).$$
(c) **Vertex.** The germ of $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{HRA}_r$ at $W_0$ is diffeomorphic to the germ at $0$ of the skew-determinantal cone $\Sigma_r=\{\Omega\in\mathfrak{so}(n):\operatorname{rank}\Omega\le r\}$, which is not linear. So $W_0$ is a singular point (the vertex) of the image. Together with (b), the paired initialisation is an **apex**.

(d) **Scope.**
- *Not a product.* (a) is a meet in the image poset (Obs I.4(c)). HRA is not the categorical product of LoRA$_r$ and OFT$_{SO}$: the set-level fibre product $\{(B,A,R):W_0+BA=W_0R\}$ has local dimension $d+r^2=rn+\tfrac{r(r-1)}2\ne rn$ over a generic point of the meet. (It is not pure-dimensional: over $W_0$ alone it contains $\{(B,0,I)\}$, of dimension $mr$.)
- *Exactly orthogonal OFT is smaller.* The Cayley map never produces a rotation with eigenvalue $-1$. For exact full-block Cayley OFT (the original paper; HF with `use_cayley_neumann=False`), $(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r})\cap\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{OFT}$ is dense in $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{HRA}_r$ but not equal to it: $W_0H_{e_1}H_{e_2}$, with $H_{e_1}H_{e_2}=\mathrm{diag}(-1,-1,1,\dots,1)$, is missing. For exact block Cayley OFT with $b<n$ the intersection is a proper subset of $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{HRA}_r$.
- *HF's default OFT is incomparable.* HF PEFT's default OFT (`use_cayley_neumann=True`) is not orthogonal (Cor II.6). Since $R^\top R=(I-Q^4)^2=I$ forces $Q=0$ near $Q=0$, its image meets $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{HRA}_r$ near $W_0$ only at $W_0$, while its intersection with $W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}$ contains non-orthogonal points such as $W_0(I+2Q+2Q^2+2Q^3+Q^4)$ with $\operatorname{rank}Q=2$.
- *Implementation.* The theorem concerns HRA with $\lambda<\infty$ (HF `apply_GS=False`). The strictly orthogonal Gram–Schmidt variant has the smaller image $W_0(I-2P_U)$, of dimension $r(n-r)$. The paired initialisation is HF's default (`repeat_interleave`) and is not stated in the HRA paper. HF HRA acts on `in_features`, so injectivity requires `out_features` $\ge$ `in_features` (and full column rank); the theorem does not cover `down_proj` or GQA key/value projections. The Gram–Schmidt variant never contains $W_0$, since $I-2P_U\ne I$, and at HF's default paired initialisation it runs Gram–Schmidt on duplicated columns, which is numerically degenerate.
proof:
*Proof.* (a) "$\subseteq$": each $H_u-I$ has rank one, so $R=\prod H_{u_i}$ fixes $\bigcap u_i^\perp$ and $\operatorname{rank}(R-I)\le r$. Also $\det R=(-1)^r=1$.

"$\supseteq$": suppose $W_0R=W_0+X$ with $\operatorname{rank}X\le r$ and $R\in SO(n)$. Injectivity gives $k':=\operatorname{rank}(R-I)\le r$. By the Cartan–Dieudonné theorem in Scherk's sharp form, $R$ is a product of exactly $k'$ reflections, and $\det R=(-1)^{k'}$ forces $k'$ to be even. Pad with $(r-k')/2$ pairs $H_uH_u=I$.

Dimension: a generic element is determined by its moved space $\mathrm{im}(R-I)\in\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$, of dimension $r(n-r)$, together with a fixed-point-free element of $SO(r)$ on it, an open set of dimension $r(r-1)/2$. The generic fibre then has dimension $rn-d$.

(b) Normalise $\hat w=w/\|w\|$. A direct computation gives
$$\tfrac{d}{d\varepsilon}\big(H_{w+\varepsilon a}H_{w+\varepsilon b}\big)\big|_0=\tfrac{2}{\|w\|}\big(v\hat w^\top-\hat wv^\top\big),\qquad v=(I-\hat w\hat w^\top)(a-b).$$
Since every pair equals $I$ at $q_0$, the differential of the product is the sum of the pair differentials. So $S_1=W_0\cdot\{\sum_iv_i\wedge\hat w_i\}$, where $v\wedge w:=vw^\top-wv^\top$.

This set is contained in $\{\Omega:P_{U^\perp}\Omega P_{U^\perp}=0\}$, because $y^\top(v\hat w^\top-\hat wv^\top)x=0$ for $x,y\perp\hat w$. Conversely, the right-hand side is spanned by $e_a\wedge e_b$ with $e_a\in U$, and each of these is a combination of the elements $\hat w_i\wedge e_b$. Its dimension is $\dim\mathfrak{so}(n)-\dim\mathfrak{so}(n-k)$, and $W_0$ is injective. Finally,
$$d-\dim S_1=k(2n-3k-1)/2>0\quad\text{for }n\ge 2k+2.$$

(c) Use the Cayley map $C(\Omega)=(I+\Omega)(I-\Omega)^{-1}$. It is a diffeomorphism from a neighbourhood of $0\in\mathfrak{so}(n)$ onto a neighbourhood of $I\in SO(n)$, and $C(\Omega)-I=2\Omega(I-\Omega)^{-1}$, so $\operatorname{rank}(C(\Omega)-I)=\operatorname{rank}\Omega$. Composing with the linear embedding $R\mapsto W_0R$ identifies the germs. $\Sigma_r$ is a closed cone. It is not linear, because a rank-$r$ and a rank-$2$ skew matrix can sum to rank $r+2\le n$. A closed cone that is $C^1$ at its vertex is linear, so $0$ is singular. The apex statement is (b): a singular image alone would not give a positive deficit.

(d) Over a generic point of the meet, the LoRA fibre is a $GL_r$-orbit and the $SO(n)$ fibre is a point, since $W_0$ is injective. If $C(\Omega)x=-x$, then $y=(I-\Omega)^{-1}x$ satisfies $(I+\Omega)y=-(I-\Omega)y$, so $y=0$. Density: perturb the angles $\pi$ inside the same moved planes. The Gram–Schmidt variant uses orthonormal $\hat u_i$, and $\prod(I-2\hat u_i\hat u_i^\top)=I-2P_U$. ∎ [Num: at $n=9$, the paired-init Jacobian has rank $8$ against generic rank $15$ for $r=2$, and $15$ against $26$ for $r=4$.]

public_statement: Let $W_0$ have full column rank (out_features $\ge$ in_features) and let $r\le n-2$ be even. Then the image of $r$-reflection HRA without Gram–Schmidt, HF PEFT's default (`apply_GS=False`), is exactly $\{W_0R:R\in SO(n),\ \operatorname{rank}(W_0R-W_0)\le r\}$, the image-level intersection of $\mathrm{LoRA}_r$ with the rotation orbit $W_0\cdot SO(n)$, of dimension $rn-r(r+1)/2$. This is a statement about images; HRA is not the categorical product of the two. At HF's default paired initialisation ($u_{2i-1}=u_{2i}$), $W_0$ is a singular vertex of the image and the first-order image has dimension $kn-k(k+1)/2$ with $k=r/2$, so that initialisation is an apex like zero-init LoRA. HRA's image strictly contains LoRA $\cap$ OFT for exactly orthogonal (Cayley) OFT; HF's default Cayley–Neumann OFT is not orthogonal, and the two are incomparable.

name: DoRA is LoRA followed by an output scale, at the level of images
statement:
**Proposition II.8 (DoRA is LoRA followed by an output scale, at the level of images).** [Prop] Assume $1\le r\le\min(m,n)$ and $s\ne0$. Let $N$ normalise rows; DoRA's magnitude $\mu\in\mathbb R^m$ is per output neuron, as in HF PEFT and the official code (the paper's notation says "column-wise", in the transposed convention). Images refer to the merged (eval-mode) weight; HF's train-mode forward with `lora_dropout`$>0$ is not of the form $Wx$. Let $W_0$ have no zero row, let $\mathcal U$ be the open set of matrices with no zero row, and let $\mathrm{Diag}_m$ be the monoid of all diagonal matrices. Then
$$\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{DoRA}_r=\{\mathrm{diag}(\mu)\,N(V):V\in(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r})\cap\mathcal U,\ \mu\in\mathbb R^m\}=\mathrm{Diag}_m\cdot(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}),$$
which is exactly the image of "LoRA$_r$ followed by a trainable output scale $\ell\in\mathbb R^m$". With $\mu$ restricted to $(\mathbb R^\times)^m$, or equivalently after intersecting with $\mathcal U$: $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{DoRA}_r\cap\mathcal U=T_m\cdot(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r})\cap\mathcal U$. Moreover:
- $d(\mathrm{DoRA}_r)\le\min\big(mn,\ r(m+n-r)+m\big)$. At a parameter point with $\mu\in(\mathbb R^\times)^m$ and $X=sBA\in\mathcal M_r$, with $U=\mathrm{col}X$ and $R=\mathrm{row}X$, the Jacobian rank is $r(m+n-r)+m-\dim\ker\big(\delta\mapsto P_{U^\perp}\mathrm{diag}(\delta)W_0P_{R^\perp}\big)$; where some $\mu_i=0$ it is smaller. For generic $W_0$, $d=\min\big(mn,\ r(m+n-r)+m\big)$; in particular $d=r(m+n-r)+m$ iff $(m-r)(n-r)\ge m$, which holds for all practical shapes. For special $W_0$ it is smaller: for $W_0=ac^\top$ with all $a_i\ne0$ and $r<n$, $d=r(m+n-r)+m-r$, strictly below the generic value iff $r<m$ and $r\le n-2$.
- The image covariance group contains $\mathrm{Mon}_m\times GL_n$.
- At $B=0$, in HF's magnitude coordinates, $\Delta W=(\mathrm{diag}(\mu_i/\|w_{0,i}\|)-I)W_0$, which can have rank up to $\operatorname{rank}W_0$, so DoRA escapes LoRA's rank bound.
proof: *Proof.* $\mathrm{diag}(\mu)N(V)=\mathrm{diag}(\mu_i/\|v_i\|)V\in\mathrm{Diag}_m\cdot V$. Conversely, take $\mathrm{diag}(\ell)V$ with $V=W_0+X$, $\operatorname{rank}X\le r$, and let $Z$ be the set of zero rows of $V$. Put $V'=W_0+(I-\varepsilon\sum_{i\in Z}E_{ii})X$. Its rows outside $Z$ are those of $V$, its rows in $Z$ are $\varepsilon w_{0,i}\ne0$, and its update still has rank $\le r$. With $\ell'_i=0$ on $Z$ and $\ell'_i=\ell_i$ elsewhere, $\mathrm{diag}(\ell')V'=\mathrm{diag}(\ell)V$ and $V'\in\mathcal U$. For the $T_m$ statement, $DV\in\mathcal U$ with $D$ invertible forces $V\in\mathcal U$. Dimension: $\varphi(\mu,B,A)=(\mu_i/\lVert v_i\rVert,B,A)$ is a diffeomorphism of DoRA's domain onto that of LoRA plus an output scale, and $\rho_{\rm DoRA}=\rho_{\text{LoRA+scale}}\circ\varphi$. The tangent space at $(D,X)$ of $(D,X)\mapsto D(W_0+X)$ is $D\big[\{\mathrm{diag}(\delta)V\}+T_X\mathcal M_r\big]$ after $\delta\mapsto D^{-1}\delta$, so for invertible $D$ it suffices to work at $(I,X)$. There $\{\mathrm{diag}(\delta)V\}$ has dimension $m$ because $V\in\mathcal U$, and $\mathrm{diag}(\delta)V\in T_X\mathcal M_r$ iff $P_{U^\perp}\mathrm{diag}(\delta)VP_{R^\perp}=0$, where $VP_{R^\perp}=W_0P_{R^\perp}$. A zero $\mu_i$ kills row $i$ of the LoRA directions, which lowers the rank further. Generic value: with bases $E$ of $U^\perp$ and $F$ of $R^\perp$ the map is $\delta\mapsto\sum_i\delta_i\,(E^\top e_i)\otimes(F^\top w_{0,i})$. For generic $(W_0,U,R)$ these are $m$ generic points of the Segre cone in $\mathbb R^{m-r}\otimes\mathbb R^{n-r}$, which is irreducible and spans the whole space, so they span $\min(m,(m-r)(n-r))$ dimensions (a standard-basis witness shows the open condition is non-empty). Since $r(m+n-r)+(m-r)(n-r)=mn$, $d=\min(mn,r(m+n-r)+m)$ off a proper algebraic subset. For $W_0=ac^\top$, the kernel is $\mathrm{diag}(a)^{-1}U$, of dimension $r$, whenever $c\notin R$. Covariance: a monomial $g$ normalises $\mathrm{Diag}_m$ and $g\mathcal M_{\le r}h^{-1}=\mathcal M_{\le r}$, so $g\,\mathrm{Diag}_m(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r})h^{-1}=\mathrm{Diag}_m(gW_0h^{-1}+\mathcal M_{\le r})$. ∎ [Num: Jacobian rank $9=mn$ at $(m,n,r)=(3,3,2)$, where the formula gives $11$; $36$ at $(8,8,2)$, matching, and $34$ there when one $\mu_i=0$; $24$ for a rank-one $W_0$ at $(6,6,2)$.]

Repaired: Im DoRA_r = Diag_m.(W0 + M_{<=r}) = image of LoRA plus an output scale (proved, so the first half of Conj D is now a theorem), with the T_m form after intersecting with matrices without zero rows; d <= min(mn, r(m+n-r)+m) with an exact kernel criterion and generic equality [Num]; the B=0 formula fixed; Conj D restated.

False as stated: the shortfall clause needs all mu_i != 0 (a zero magnitude lowers the rank: 34, not 36, at (8,8,2)); the rank-one value needs r < n and is strictly below generic only for r < m, r <= n-2; r <= min(m,n) and s != 0 were implicit. public_statement: For a linear layer whose frozen weight $W_0$ has no zero rows, and $r\le\min(m,n)$, DoRA as implemented in HF PEFT (one unconstrained magnitude per output neuron) reaches exactly the same merged weights as rank-$r$ LoRA followed by a free per-output-neuron gain, $\{\mathrm{diag}(\ell)(W_0+X):\operatorname{rank}X\le r\}$. This set has dimension $\min(mn,\,r(m+n-r)+m)$ for generic $W_0$ and less for special $W_0$, for example $r(m+n-r)+m-r$ when $W_0$ has rank one. So DoRA buys no expressivity beyond LoRA plus $m$ output gains. Any difference from that baseline, starting from the same weights, comes from training dynamics, namely the row-normalised parametrisation, DoRA's detached-norm backward, and the way the optimizer treats the magnitude coordinates.

name: the torus ladder
statement:
**Proposition II.9 (the torus ladder).** [Prop]

(a) **HiRA.** $\rho(B,A)=W_0\odot(J+BA)$, where $J$ is the all-ones matrix; HF PEFT has $B_0=0$ and no scale factor on Linear and Conv layers (on embeddings it uses $A_0=0$). For every $W_0$, $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{HiRA}_r=W_0+D_{W_0}(\mathcal M_{\le r})$ with $D_{W_0}:X\mapsto W_0\odot X$. If $W_0$ has no zero entries, $D_{W_0}\in GL(\Theta)$, so inside the slice at $\theta_0$ HiRA is LoRA transported by a diagonal automorphism: it has the same $d=r(m+n-r)$ (for $r\le\min(m,n)$) and the same gauge. In all cases $\operatorname{rank}\Delta W\le r\cdot\operatorname{rank}W_0$. The transport depends on $\theta_0$ (Prop II.13).

(b) **Scalings.** Output-side scalings, $\mathrm{diag}(\ell)W_0=W_0\odot(J+(\ell-\mathbf 1)\mathbf 1^\top)$, and input-side scalings, $W_0\mathrm{diag}(\ell)=W_0\odot(J+\mathbf 1(\ell-\mathbf 1)^\top)$, have images in $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{HiRA}_1$. Output-side examples: (IA)$^3$ on keys and values, the post-linear scale of SSF, DoRA's magnitude. Input-side examples: (IA)$^3$'s feed-forward vector, which scales the input of $W_{\rm down}$, and a LayerNorm gain $\gamma$ folded into the next linear map. The fold is exact when the norm's output is consumed only by linear maps: the input norms of pre-norm blocks, and a final norm before an untied head (in post-norm BERT, the last block's norm feeds only the head). It does not apply to Gemma-style post-sublayer norms, which HF's default LN-tuning targets for Gemma 2 and 3, to QK-norms, or to post-norm residual paths. Where it applies, $\gamma$ is tied across all consumers of the norm (Q, K and V, or gate and up) rather than being a free point per box, and with tied embeddings a fold into the head breaks the tie. LayerNorm biases and SSF's shift fold into the next bias, not into $W$. Two-sided scalings $\mathrm{diag}(a)W_0\mathrm{diag}(b)=W_0\odot(ab^\top)$ lie in $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{HiRA}_2$. As a morphism, $h(\ell)=(\ell-\mathbf 1,\mathbf 1^\top)$ lands in $\mathrm{HiRA}_1$ pointed at $(0,\mathbf 1^\top)$, which is not HiRA's random-$A$ default pointing.

(c) **Orbit dimension.** The two-sided torus orbit $\{\mathrm{diag}(a)W_0\mathrm{diag}(b)\}$ has dimension $m+n-c(W_0)$, where $c(W_0)$ is the number of connected components of the bipartite support graph of $W_0$, an isolated vertex counting as its own component.

(d) **RoAd.** RoAd$_1$ (the paper's main variant, HF `road_1`) is $W=RW_0$ with $R$ block-diagonal in scaled rotations $\alpha_i\mathrm{Rot}(\theta_i)$ of output pairs. It is the left action of $CO^+(2)^{m/2}\cong(\mathbb C^\times)^{m/2}$: it is **(IA)$^3$ over $\mathbb C$**. It multiplies the input Gram matrix of each output pair by $\alpha_i^2$. Since $\alpha_i$ may be $0$, its image is the orbit closure, a real-linear space of dimension exactly $m$ whenever no output-pair block of $W_0$ is zero. RoAd$_2$ and RoAd$_4$ (HF `road_2`, `road_4`) let each block range over all of $M_2(\mathbb R)$. They realise the block-diagonal action of the monoid $M_2(\mathbb R)^{m/2}$ (its group part $GL_2^{m/2}$ is non-abelian), with linear image $\{\mathrm{blockdiag}(R_i)W_0\}$ of dimension $2m$ when every pair block has rank $2$. For them the Gram statement and "over $\mathbb C$" fail, and RoAd$_4$ carries a positive-dimensional gauge (two dimensions per row). HF pairs output $j$ with $j+g/2$ inside each group of size $g$ (default $64$) rather than adjacent outputs as in the paper, and also rotates the bias; the statements above do not depend on the pairing.

(e) **Zeros and covariance.** Every $W$ reachable by HiRA, (IA)$^3$ or SSF vanishes wherever $W_0$ does, $Z(W_0)\subseteq Z(W)$, and this persists under merging. New zeros can appear ($\ell_i=0$, or $(J+BA)_{ij}=0$), so the zero pattern itself is not invariant. The image covariance group of output-scaled boxes ((IA)$^3$ on $k,v$; post-linear SSF) is $\mathrm{Mon}_m\times GL_n$, and that of input-scaled boxes ((IA)$^3$ on $W_{\rm down}$) is $GL_m\times\mathrm{Mon}_n$. HiRA's is exactly $\mathrm{Mon}_m\times\mathrm{Mon}_n$ ($=GL_1\times GL_1$ when $m=n=1$).
proof:
*Proof.* (a) $W_0\odot(J+BA)=W_0+W_0\odot BA$. $D_{W_0}$ is diagonal in the standard basis of $\Theta$, and invertible iff no entry vanishes. Pushforward along a linear isomorphism preserves dimension and gauge. For the rank, $W_0\odot(BA)=\sum_k\mathrm{diag}(b_k)W_0\mathrm{diag}(a_k)$, which has rank $\le r\operatorname{rank}W_0$.

(b) Direct computation, using $ab^\top-J=[a,-\mathbf 1][b,\mathbf 1]^\top\in\mathcal M_{\le2}$.

(c) The tangent map at $(\mathbf 1,\mathbf 1)$ is $(\alpha,\beta)\mapsto\big((\alpha_i+\beta_j)(W_0)_{ij}\big)$. Its kernel requires $\alpha_i+\beta_j=0$ along every support edge, so it is one-dimensional on each connected component. Torus orbits are homogeneous, so the dimension is the same at every point of the orbit.

(d) A $2\times n$ real block $X$ is a complex row in $\mathbb C^n$, and $\alpha\mathrm{Rot}(\theta)$ acts on it as multiplication by $\alpha e^{i\theta}$. So the image for one pair is $\mathbb C\cdot X$, of real dimension $2$ iff $X\ne0$, and $(\alpha\mathrm{Rot}X)^\top(\alpha\mathrm{Rot}X)=\alpha^2X^\top X$. In RoAd$_2$ each row of a block is an arbitrary vector of $\mathbb R^2$ written in polar form.

(e) Hadamard multiplication and row or column scaling preserve the zeros of $W_0$.

*(IA)$^3$ and SSF.* A monomial $g$ normalises the diagonal monoid, so $\mathrm{Mon}_m\times GL_n$ is contained in the covariance group of output scalings. Conversely, take $W_0=e_jc^\top$. Then $\mathrm{Im}\,M(gW_0h^{-1})=\mathrm{span}\{e_i:i\in\mathrm{supp}(ge_j)\}\,c^\top h^{-1}$, while $g\,\mathrm{Im}\,M(W_0)\,h^{-1}=\mathbb R\,(ge_j)c^\top h^{-1}$. Equality forces $\lvert\mathrm{supp}(ge_j)\rvert=1$ for every $j$, so $g$ is monomial. This works for all $m,n$. Input-side scalings are the transpose.

*HiRA.* Monomial pairs commute with Hadamard products up to relabelling. Conversely, take $W_0=E_{ij}$, so that $\mathrm{Im}\,M(E_{ij})=\mathbb RE_{ij}$, and put $u=ge_i$, $v=h^{-\top}e_j$. Covariance would force $\mathrm{Im}\,M(uv^\top)=uv^\top\odot(J+\mathcal M_{\le r})$ to be the line $\mathbb R\,uv^\top$. It contains $uv^\top+t\,u_kv_lE_{kl}$ for every $(k,l)$ in the support of $uv^\top$, so it has dimension at least $2$ unless $\lvert\mathrm{supp}\,u\rvert=\lvert\mathrm{supp}\,v\rvert=1$. This holds for every $i,j$ only when $g$ and $h$ are monomial. ∎ [Num: RoAd$_1$ orbit dimension $8$ and RoAd$_2$ dimension $16$ at $m=8$.]
referee_notes: Mathematics of (a)-(c) confirmed. Defects: RoAd as stated covers only RoAd_1 (RoAd_2/4 have arbitrary 2x2 blocks, a non-abelian GL_2 action with image of dimension 2m); CO(2) should be CO^+(2); folding a LayerNorm gain needs a pre-norm architecture and is tied across consumers; the (IA)^3 FFN vector scales the input of W_down (covariance GL x Mon); 'the zero pattern is an absolute invariant' is false (only Z(W0) is contained in Z(W)); 'never GL x GL' fails at m=n=1; the (IA)^3 covariance proof assumed full row rank. All repaired: the (IA)^3 proof now uses W0 = e_j c^T for all m, n, and the ladder gloss was toned down.
round2_notes: Round 2 (math minor, faithful minor): no false mathematical claim. Fixed: d = r(m+n-r) needs r <= min(m,n); HF HiRA embeddings use A_0 = 0; HiRA's covariance group is now proved to be exactly Mon_m x Mon_n (test at W_0 = E_ij); RoAd_2/4 is a monoid action (group part GL_2^{m/2}), with a note on HF's (j, j+g/2) pairing and bias rotation. The LayerNorm fold is restricted to norms whose output feeds only linear maps (not Gemma-style post-sublayer norms, QK-norms or post-norm residual paths), and biases and SSF's shift fold into the next bias. The gloss now says only the scaling methods are rungs; DoRA and RoAd are rungs only for zero-free W_0, and RoAd lies on no low-rank rung only for generic W_0.
public_statement: In HF PEFT's HiRA, $W=W_0\odot(J+BA)$ with $B_0=0$ and no scale factor, so the reachable set is $W_0+W_0\odot\{\operatorname{rank}\le r\}$. For $W_0$ with no zero entries this is LoRA's image moved by the invertible diagonal map $X\mapsto W_0\odot X$, with the same dimension $r(m+n-r)$ (for $r\le\min(m,n)$) and the same gauge. In general $\operatorname{rank}\Delta W\le r\operatorname{rank}W_0$, an entry that is zero in $W_0$ stays zero, and the image covariance group is exactly $\mathrm{Mon}_m\times\mathrm{Mon}_n$. One-sided rescalings ((IA)$^3$ vectors, SSF's scales, DoRA's magnitude with $B=0$, and the gain of a LayerNorm that feeds only linear maps) lie in the image of rank-1 HiRA, and two-sided rescalings in that of rank-2 HiRA. RoAd$_1$ is a complex scaling of output pairs, with an $m$-dimensional linear image, and RoAd$_2$/RoAd$_4$ apply arbitrary $2\times2$ blocks, with a linear image of dimension up to $2m$.

name: cut-rank bound
statement:
**Theorem II.10 (cut-rank bound).** [Thm; standard] Let $\Gamma$ be a tensor network, evaluated in the symmetric monoidal category $(\mathbf{FinVect},\otimes)$, with input legs $V$ and output legs $U$. Every wire and open leg is assumed incident to a vertex: insert an identity box on any bare strand, or equivalently count each bare input–output wire as crossing every cut. A crossing hyperedge (copy spider) contributes its dimension once. Partition the vertices into $\mathcal I\sqcup\mathcal O$. The weight $w$ of the cut is the product of the dimensions of the internal wires between the two sides and of the open legs attached on the wrong side (input legs at $\mathcal O$, output legs at $\mathcal I$). Then
$$\operatorname{rank}[\![\Gamma]\!]\le\min_{\rm cuts}w,$$
and rank is subadditive over formal sums. The bound refers to a chosen presentation of the network.
proof: *Proof.* Write $V_{\mathcal I},V_{\mathcal O}$ for the input legs attached to $\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal O$, $U_{\mathcal I},U_{\mathcal O}$ likewise for the outputs, and $C$ for the tensor product of the cut wires. Contracting each side gives $T_{\mathcal I}:V_{\mathcal I}\to U_{\mathcal I}\otimes C$ and $T_{\mathcal O}:C\otimes V_{\mathcal O}\to U_{\mathcal O}$. Then $[\![\Gamma]\!]=(\mathrm{id}_{U_{\mathcal I}}\otimes T_{\mathcal O})\circ(T_{\mathcal I}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{V_{\mathcal O}})$ factors through $U_{\mathcal I}\otimes C\otimes V_{\mathcal O}$, of dimension $w$. Symmetric monoidal structure suffices; no cups or caps are needed. Subadditivity is $\operatorname{rank}(X+Y)\le\operatorname{rank}X+\operatorname{rank}Y$. ∎ [Num: no violation in 283 random networks.]
referee_notes: Both referees: the cut bound is correct under the standard convention. Wording repaired: bare input-to-output strands must be incident to a vertex (otherwise I_d (x) BA is a counterexample); hyperedges count once; the proof is rewritten as (id (x) T_O) o (T_I (x) id) through U_I (x) C (x) V_O; symmetric monoidal structure suffices (no compact closure). Consequences now say that the bound refers to a presentation (HRA and Givens via the telescoping sum, HiRA via factoring W0), that splitting inits give 2r, that FourierFT <= min(2n_c, m, n), and that a large min-cut is necessary but not sufficient.
round2_notes: Not covered by round 2; round-1 status kept.
public_statement: For a tensor network evaluated in finite-dimensional vector spaces, the rank of the map it computes is at most the smallest product of wire dimensions across any cut that separates inputs from outputs, and rank is subadditive over sums. This reads the maximum rank of a structured adapter off its diagram, for a chosen presentation of the network.

name: Kronecker incomparability
statement:
**Theorem II.11 (Kronecker incomparability).** [Thm; linear algebra standard (Van Loan–Pitsianis, operator-Schmidt decomposition); PEFT reading new] Write $\mathbb R^m=\mathbb R^{m_1}\otimes\mathbb R^{m_2}$ and $\mathbb R^n=\mathbb R^{n_1}\otimes\mathbb R^{n_2}$, and view $\Delta\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ as a 4-leg tensor. Let $\operatorname{rk}$ be the rank across the cut $\{U_1U_2\}\mid\{V_1V_2\}$ and $\operatorname{rk}_\otimes$ the rank across $\{U_1V_1\}\mid\{U_2V_2\}$.

(a) $\operatorname{rk}_\otimes\Delta\le k$ iff $\Delta=\sum_{i\le k}C_i\otimes D_i$. Every $\Delta$ has $\operatorname{rk}_\otimes\Delta\le\min(m_1n_1,m_2n_2)$.

(b) $\operatorname{rk}(C\otimes D)=\operatorname{rk}C\cdot\operatorname{rk}D$, while $\operatorname{rk}_\otimes(C\otimes D)=1$ for $C,D\ne0$.

(c) If $u\in\mathbb R^m$ and $v\in\mathbb R^n$ have Schmidt ranks $\rho_u,\rho_v$, then $\operatorname{rk}_\otimes(uv^\top)=\rho_u\rho_v$. A generic rank-one update therefore has Kronecker rank $\kappa_1:=\min(m_1,m_2)\cdot\min(n_1,n_2)$. For aligned splits, $(m_1-m_2)(n_1-n_2)\ge0$, which include equal square splits and every split HF PEFT's factorisation produces (it puts the smaller factor first on both sides), $\kappa_1=\min(m_1n_1,m_2n_2)$ is the maximal Kronecker rank.

(d) **Incomparability.** Put $\nu:=\min(m_1,n_1)\min(m_2,n_2)$, the largest rank of a single Kronecker product. For $1\le r<\nu$ and $1\le k<\kappa_1$, the sets $\mathcal M_{\le r}$ and $\mathcal K_{\le k}:=\{\Delta:\operatorname{rk}_\otimes\Delta\le k\}$ of unconstrained $k$-term Kronecker sums are incomparable, for every split: a generic rank-one update lies in the first and not the second, and $C\otimes D$ with full-rank factors, of Kronecker rank $1$ and rank $\nu$, lies in the second and not the first. For equal square splits ($m=n=N$, all factors $s$), $\kappa_1=\nu=s^2=N$, and $I_N$ is such a product.

(e) **Constrained Kronecker methods.** Let $\mathrm{Im}\,M\subseteq W_0+\mathcal K_{\le k}$. Then $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{LoRA}_r\not\subseteq\mathrm{Im}\,M$ whenever $k<\kappa_1$, for every pointing of $\mathrm{LoRA}_r$. Give $\mathrm{LoRA}_r$ its zero-init pointing, with image $W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}$. Then $\mathrm{Im}\,M\not\subseteq\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{LoRA}_r$ iff some $\theta\in\mathrm{Im}\,M$ has $\operatorname{rank}(\theta-W_0)>r$. For LoKr, $C\otimes BA$ with $C\in\mathbb R^{m_1\times n_1}$, $B\in\mathbb R^{m_2\times r'}$ and $A\in\mathbb R^{r'\times n_2}$, put $r'_{\rm eff}=\min(r',m_2,n_2)$. The maximum rank is $\min(m_1,n_1)\cdot r'_{\rm eff}$. So $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{LoKr}_{r'}\subseteq\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{LoRA}_r$ iff $r\ge\min(m_1,n_1)r'_{\rm eff}$, and otherwise the two images are incomparable, provided $\kappa_1>1$. In HF PEFT the second LoKr factor is low-rank only when $r<\max(m_2,n_2)/2$; otherwise it is full and LoKr is unconstrained KronA, with maximum rank $\min(m_1,n_1)\min(m_2,n_2)$. On a $768$-wide layer ($24\times32$) the maximum rank therefore jumps from $360$ at $r=15$ to $768$ at $r=16$. With `decompose_both`, $C$ is also capped at rank $r$.
proof: *Proof.* (a) and (b) follow from the Van Loan–Pitsianis rearrangement $\mathcal R(C\otimes D)=\mathrm{vec}C\,\mathrm{vec}D^\top$, which is wire-bending; $\mathcal R\Delta$ is an $(m_1n_1)\times(m_2n_2)$ matrix. For (c), write the Schmidt decompositions $u=\sum\sigma_ix_i\otimes y_i$ and $v=\sum\tau_jz_j\otimes w_j$. Then $uv^\top=\sum_{ij}\sigma_i\tau_j(x_iz_j^\top)\otimes(y_iw_j^\top)$ is an operator-Schmidt decomposition with Frobenius-orthonormal families and $\rho_u\rho_v$ nonzero coefficients; generic $u,v$ have full Schmidt ranks. Under alignment $\min(m_1,m_2)\min(n_1,n_2)=\min(m_1n_1,m_2n_2)$, which is the bound of (a). (d) follows from (b) and (c) and needs no alignment. The second clause is the definition of $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{LoRA}_r$. For LoKr, $\operatorname{rank}(C\otimes BA)=\operatorname{rk}C\cdot\operatorname{rk}(BA)\le\min(m_1,n_1)\,r'_{\rm eff}$ by (b), with equality for full-rank $C$ and $BA$ of rank $r'_{\rm eff}$; $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{LoRA}_r\not\subseteq\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{LoKr}$ because $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{LoKr}\subseteq W_0+\mathcal K_{\le1}$ and $1<\kappa_1$. ∎ [Num: Schmidt ranks $(1,3)\to3$, $(2,3)\to6$, $(3,3)\to9$, each with ordinary rank $1$; for the $2\times4$ split of $\mathbb R^8$, $\operatorname{rk}_\otimes(uv^\top)=4$, the maximal Kronecker rank; LoKr with $s=4$, $r'=1$ never exceeds rank $4$; at $(m_1,m_2,n_1,n_2)=(2,8,8,2)$ with inner dimension $4$, LoKr never exceeds rank $4=\min(m_1,n_1)\,r'_{\rm eff}$.]

public_statement: Split the dimensions as $m=m_1m_2$ and $n=n_1n_2$. A $k$-term Kronecker sum $\sum C_i\otimes D_i$ is exactly a rank-$\le k$ matrix after the Van Loan–Pitsianis rearrangement, so unconstrained Kronecker methods are LoRA across a different cut of the same 4-leg tensor. A generic rank-one update has Kronecker rank $\min(m_1,m_2)\min(n_1,n_2)$, which is the largest possible for aligned splits, including equal square splits and every split HF PEFT's factorisation produces. So zero-init $\mathrm{LoRA}_r$ and Kronecker sums with fewer terms than that have incomparable images whenever $r$ is below the rank $\min(m_1,n_1)\min(m_2,n_2)$ of a full-rank single Kronecker product. LoKr updates $C\otimes BA$ with inner rank $r'\le\min(m_2,n_2)$ have rank at most $\min(m_1,n_1)r'$, attained, so LoKr's image lies inside zero-init $\mathrm{LoRA}_r$ iff $r\ge\min(m_1,n_1)r'$ and is incomparable with it otherwise (when $\min(m_1,m_2)\min(n_1,n_2)>1$). In HF PEFT the second LoKr factor is low-rank only when $r<\max(m_2,n_2)/2$; above that LoKr is an unconstrained Kronecker product.

name: gauge census: rank is a cut, dimension is a volume
statement:
**Proposition II.12 (gauge census: rank is a cut, dimension is a volume).** [Prop]

(a) $d(M)\le\lvert M\rvert-\dim(\text{generic gauge orbit})$, with equality when the gauge acts locally transitively on generic fibres.

(b) The following values hold for one $m\times n$ box, with $r\le\min(m,n)$ throughout except for VeRA (whose published RoBERTa-base setting has $r=1024>768$). The gauge column lists the exhibited Lie group; it is locally transitive on generic fibres away from the $mn$ cap, but not where the cap binds (for LoHa at $(4,4,2)$ the orbit has dimension $15$ and the fibre $16$).

| method | budget $\lvert M\rvert$ | exhibited Lie gauge (orbit dim) | $d(M)$ | max rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LoRA$_r$ | $r(m+n)$ | $GL_r$ ($r^2$) | $r(m+n-r)$ | $r$ |
| GraLoRA ($k\times k$ blocks, rank $r/k$ each; HF default `hybrid_r=0`) | $r(m+n)$ | $\prod GL_{r/k}$ ($r^2$) | $r(m+n-r)$ | $\min(kr,m,n)$ |
| LoHa$_{r_1,r_2}$ | $(r_1+r_2)(m+n)$ | $GL_{r_1}\times GL_{r_2}\times$ diagonal torus ($r_1^2+r_2^2+m+n-1$) | $\min\big(mn,\ r_1(m+n-r_1)+r_2(m+n-r_2)-(m+n-1)\big)$ [Num; the second argument is an upper bound] | $\min(r_1r_2,m,n)$ |
| HRA$_r$ ($\operatorname{rank}W_0=n$, `apply_GS=False`; even $r$ is needed only for HF's identity init) | $rn$ | non-linear; fibre dimension $r(r+1)/2$; exhibited Lie gauge $(\mathbb R^\times)^r$ | $rn-r(r+1)/2$ (for $r\in\{n-1,n\}$ this is $\dim SO(n)$ [Num]) | $r$ |
| DoRA$_r$ | $r(m+n)+m$ | $GL_r$ for generic $W_0$ with $(m-r)(n-r)\ge m$ (larger otherwise: dimension $6>r^2$ at $(3,3,2)$, and $r^2+r$ for rank-one $W_0$) | $\min\big(mn,\ r(m+n-r)+m\big)$ for generic $W_0$ (Prop II.8) | up to full |
| VeRA | $m+r$ | $\mathbb R^\times$ | $m+r-1$ [Num] | $\min(r,m,n)$ |
| KronA $A\otimes B$ | $m_1n_1+m_2n_2$ | $\mathbb R^\times$ | $m_1n_1+m_2n_2-1$ | $\min(m_1,n_1)\min(m_2,n_2)$ |
| TT / Tucker (admissible, minimal ranks) | $\sum$ cores | $\prod_eGL_{r_e}$ | $\lvert M\rvert-\sum_er_e^2$ (Tucker: Koch–Lubich, Uschmajew–Vandereycken; TT: Holtz–Rohwedder–Schneider) | up to full |
| linear methods (LoRA-FA, LoRA-XS, MiSS in every HF mode, FourierFT, C3A, masks) | $\lvert M\rvert$ | translations by the kernel | rank of the linear map; $=\lvert M\rvert$ when injective | varies |

BitFit does not touch the $m\times n$ box; it is linear in the biases. Hybrid GraLoRA (`hybrid_r>0`) is not covered by the table.

FourierFT is injective only when its sampled frequencies contain no conjugate pair $(u,v),(-u,-v)$; otherwise $d=\lvert M\rvert-\#\{\text{pairs}\}$. At LLM sizes this is close to $\lvert M\rvert$, but at $768\times768$ with $1000$ frequencies a pair occurs in about half of the draws (HF's default seed $777$ gives exactly two pairs there).

(c) **Equal-budget trades.** Assume $2r\le\min(m,n)$, $r^2\le\min(m,n)$ and $2r^2<m+n-1$. LoHa$_{r,r}$ and LoRA$_{2r}$ both cost $2r(m+n)$, but LoHa reaches at least $(m+n-1)-2r^2$ *fewer* dimensions (exactly that many [Num]). For $r\ge3$ it gains rank up to $r^2>2r$ in exchange. For $r\le2$, $r^2\le2r$, so $\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{LoHa}_{r,r}\subsetneq\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{LoRA}_{2r}$: LoHa is strictly dominated. When $2r^2\ge m+n-1$ there is no trade: LoHa$_{r,r}$ matches or exceeds LoRA$_{2r}$ in dimension as well as in rank, for instance at $(m,n,r)=(9,9,3)$, at $r=64$ on $4096\times4096$, and at LyCORIS-style $r=32$ on $320$- to $640$-wide layers. GraLoRA$_k$ costs the same as LoRA$_r$, reaches the same number of dimensions, and has maximum rank $\min(kr,m,n)$, but caps every block at rank $r/k$. A generic rank-$r$ update has rank $r$ on every block, so for $k\ge2$ and $r\le\min(m,n)/k$ the images of LoRA$_r$ and GraLoRA$_k$ are incomparable.
proof:
*Proof.* (a) The generic fibre contains the generic gauge orbit, and $d=\lvert M\rvert-\dim(\text{generic fibre})$.

The LoHa torus acts by $(B_1,A_1,B_2,A_2)\mapsto(D_1B_1,A_1D_2,D_1^{-1}B_2,A_2D_2^{-1})$. It preserves the product because $(D_1XD_2)\odot(D_1^{-1}YD_2^{-1})=X\odot Y$. At generic parameters, the joint action of $GL_{r_1}\times GL_{r_2}\times T_m\times T_n$ has a one-dimensional stabiliser, $\{(cI,c^{-1}I,cI,c^{-1}I)\}$: if $D_1B_1=B_1g_1$ for generic $B_1$ with $m>r_1$, every row of $B_1$ is a left eigenvector of $g_1$, so $g_1=cI$ and $D_1=cI$, and the other three equations force $D_2=c^{-1}I$ and $g_2=c^{-1}I$. So the orbit has dimension $r_1^2+r_2^2+m+n-1$, which gives the upper bound by (a). Trivially $d\le mn$.

GraLoRA's image is a product of $k^2$ cones $\mathcal M_{\le r/k}(\tfrac mk\times\tfrac nk)$, of total dimension $k^2\cdot\tfrac rk\cdot\tfrac{m+n-r}{k}=r(m+n-r)$. For the rank, write block $(i,j)$ as $U_{ij}V_{ij}^\top$ with $U_{ij}\in\mathbb R^{m/k\times r/k}$ and $V_{ij}\in\mathbb R^{n/k\times r/k}$. Then $\Delta W=\mathrm{blockdiag}(L_1,\dots,L_k)\,S$, with $L_i=[U_{i1}\cdots U_{ik}]\in\mathbb R^{m/k\times r}$ and $S\in\mathbb R^{kr\times n}$ stacking the $V_{ij}^\top$, each supported on column block $j$. For generic blocks and $r\le\min(m,n)/k$, each $L_i$ has full column rank $r$ and $S$ has full row rank $kr$, so $\operatorname{rank}\Delta W=kr$. In general the rank is at most $\min(kr,m,n)$. (Placing rank-$r/k$ blocks only on the diagonal gives rank $r$, not $kr$.)

LoHa$_{r,r}$ maps into LoRA$_{r^2}$ (the face-splitting arrow of Exposé VIII.C), which gives domination for $r\le2$. Under $2r^2<m+n-1$ the LoHa upper bound is $2r(m+n-2r)-\big((m+n-1)-2r^2\big)<d(\mathrm{LoRA}_{2r})\le mn$, so the cap does not bind, the gap is at least $(m+n-1)-2r^2>0$, and strictness follows. Conversely, when $2r^2\ge m+n-1$ the bound no longer separates them. The KronA image is a Segre cone. HRA is Thm II.7. The remaining rows are standard; for FourierFT, $\mathrm{Re}\circ\mathrm{ifft2}$ sends the frequencies $p$ and $-p$ to the same real pattern. ∎ [Num: LoHa $38,59,93,101$ at $(m,n,r)=(8,7,2),(12,10,2),(12,10,3),(20,16,2)$, and $16=mn$ at $(4,4,2)$, where the formula gives $17$ and $d(\mathrm{LoRA}_4)=16$ too; LoHa$_{3,3}$ against LoRA$_6$: $73$ against $72$ at $(9,9,3)$; GraLoRA dimension $48,64,108$ at $(m,n,r,k)=(8,8,4,2),(12,8,4,2),(12,12,6,3)$; GraLoRA generic rank $8=kr$ at $(16,16,4,2)$ and $12=\min(m,n)$ at $(12,12,6,3)$.]
