Repaired: Frobenius stated pointwise on an open set; dynamic hypotheses separated (continuous time, affine leaves for discrete steps, frame and metric conditions); instances and 'What this explains' rewritten; the Exposé 0 claim toned down.
round2_notes: Round 2 (math refuted, major; faithful refuted, major): the Frobenius core holds. False: (1) 'full-batch GaLore with T=1 is integrable when its rank is 1' (for r = 1 the bracket's normal part is generically nonzero; closed form at W = diag(2,1)); the 1e-9 figure only reproduces for n = 1 or single-sample least squares; (2) 'a curved metric is reproduced by no rho with constant Lambda' holds only for immersions with dim Q = rank D (counterexample: BB^T induces the curved Bures-Wasserstein metric; balanced LoRA too), and Thm III.3(a) did not prove it; (3) Flora as published is not a constant-anchor backward method. Repaired: GaLore claim restated (involutive iff U_r is invariant along D; generic failure for every r >= 1; right projection noted); flatness restated with c = M a^T and the immersion hypothesis, with a direct proof; discrete SGD needs rho affine along horizontals; continuous-time bullet assumes involutivity; the discrete iff quantifies over all optimizer outputs and intersects with U. Instances restate Prop IV.2's optimizer hypotheses (LISA's AdamW decay violates them), MeZO up to SPSA, T=1 vacuous; Flora, APOLLO and Fira are named as outside Def IV.1. Num corrected and backed by framework_checks.py.
public_statement: By Frobenius' theorem, a smooth constant-rank anchor distribution on an open set of weight space is foliated by images of injective immersions exactly when it is involutive; a single integral manifold implies nothing off itself. GaLore (any projector), LISA and MeZO keep their anchor fixed within each period, so the condition holds trivially and does not tell them apart; with weight decay $0$ and the optimizer hypotheses of Prop IV.2 they are rebasing schemes of linear forward methods. The condition has content only for anchors that depend on the weights, and the full-batch top-$r$ gradient-subspace field is generically non-involutive for every $r\ge1$ once both matrix dimensions are at least $2$. Flora as published (Adafactor base), APOLLO and Fira make updates outside their projected subspace and are not covered.

name: backward reach and the backprop cone
statement:
**Observation IV.4 (backward reach and the backprop cone).** [Obs; an upper bound] Assume reverse mode with per-box residuals only (no inter-box checkpointing), with boxes taken at the granularity where adapters are separate boxes (for LoRA-FA, $A_0$ and $B$ separately). Then it suffices to keep a VJP residual, meaning an input, an output, a sufficient statistic such as a ReLU mask, or a recipe to recompute one of these inside the box, for
- each trainable box whose parameter-VJP depends on its input: linear and multiplicative boxes such as $W$, $A$, $B$ and (IA)$^3$ scales; additive boxes such as biases and prompts need nothing;
- each *nonlinear* box on a directed path from a trainable box to the loss.

Deterministic frozen linear boxes, and all boxes off this cone, need nothing; stochastic linear boxes on the cone (dropout) need their mask or RNG state. The $k$ coordinates of $P^\top\nabla L$ can be computed exactly by $k$ forward-mode JVPs, with no reverse pass and $O(1)$-layer activation memory, each JVP costing a small constant multiple (about $1.5$ to $3$) of a forward pass. This always uses less activation memory than un-checkpointed reverse mode, but it is time-competitive with one VJP (about $3$ forward passes) only for $k$ of about $1$ or $2$. It also needs $P$ before the passes, so it cannot produce GaLore's SVD refresh more cheaply than a backward pass ($\nabla L$ itself would take $\lvert\theta\rvert$ JVPs).
proof: *Proof.* Cotangents are needed only on the downstream cone of the trainable boxes, so everything else can be pruned. A frozen linear box has $\mathsf R[f](x,y)=W^\top y$, which does not depend on $x$, whereas a nonlinear box's reverse derivative depends on its input through some residual. The parameter-VJP of a trainable linear box is $yx^\top$ (of a multiplicative scale, $\sum y\odot x$), so it needs the input $x$; a bias's parameter cotangent is its incoming cotangent; a dropout box's VJP is $\mathrm{mask}\odot y/(1-p)$. The $i$-th coordinate of $P^\top\nabla L$ is the directional derivative $DL(\theta)[p_i]$, and forward-mode AD computes it alongside one forward pass with a constant-factor overhead and $O(1)$-layer memory. MeZO's central difference has bias $O(\varepsilon^2)$ when $L$ has a Lipschitz Hessian. ∎
referee_notes: Refuted as a necessity claim: additive trainable boxes (BitFit, prompts) need no stored input; residuals can be outputs, masks or recomputation; dropout needs its mask; 'k JVPs and no VJP' omitted that this is competitive only for k = O(1) (GaLore's k is huge and its SVD refresh needs a VJP); MeZO's central difference has O(eps^2) bias for grad L; LISA always trains the embedding and LM head, so its cone is the whole network. Repaired: stated as an upper bound with explicit hypotheses and a residual notion; JVP trade-off stated; MeZO, LISA, LST and prompt-tuning readings corrected.
round2_notes: Round 2 (math minor; faithful refuted on a commentary sentence, minor): the upper bound holds and was checked against autograd. False: 'LISA's savings are in gradients and optimizer state, not activations' contradicts the Observation (frozen linears on the cone drop their input residuals; about 20% per unsampled block at LLaMA proportions) and the LISA paper. Repaired: LISA reading corrected. Also fixed: the no-rematerialisation hypothesis no longer contradicts recomputation recipes; dropout needs its mask or RNG state, on the cone only; JVP cost stated as a constant multiple of a forward pass, time-competitive only for k of about 1-2, always better on activation memory; 'unavailable' for GaLore's refresh softened to infeasible; proof gains the parameter-VJP and dropout lines and the Lipschitz-Hessian condition for MeZO. Commentary: LoRA-FA's saving needs lora_dropout = 0; 'largest cone' is the maximal cone shared with layer-1 methods; HF reentrant checkpointing note; 'memory column' renamed.
public_statement: In reverse-mode autodiff with per-box residuals only, a PEFT method needs stored activations only for trainable ops whose parameter gradient reads their input (linear or multiplicative adapters, not biases or prompts) and for nonlinear, including bilinear, ops downstream of some trainable op. Frozen deterministic linear layers and everything below the lowest trainable op need none; dropout on the cone needs its mask. This is why ladder side-tuning skips the backbone's backward pass, why LoRA-FA keeps $A_0x$ instead of $x$, why adapting only the top layers truncates backprop while training the embedding (LISA, prompt tuning) does not, and why LISA still saves the input residuals of its frozen layers. Alternatively, $k$ fixed directions of the gradient can be computed exactly by $k$ forward-mode JVPs with $O(1)$-layer memory, at a constant multiple of $k$ forward passes; that is time-competitive with one backward pass only for very small $k$, and the directions must be fixed in advance.

name: quantisation and splitting
statement:
**Proposition V.2 (quantisation and splitting).** [Prop] Write $W$ for the full-precision weight, $\kappa$ for the quantiser, $e=\kappa W-W$, and $\delta_0=\delta(q_0)$.

(a) Additive families commute with translation: $M(\theta+v)=\tau_v\circ M(\theta)$. Hence QLoRA is LoRA pointed at $\kappa\theta_0$, with defect $e$; it needs no new weight-space structure. Since $-e$ is generically of full rank, $\theta_0\notin\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{LoRA}_r(\kappa\theta_0)$ unless $\operatorname{rank}e\le r$.

(b) For splitting families derived from an SVD or from data, the order of operations matters, and three orders occur in practice:
- *split, then quantise the residual* (QPiSSA; HF's recommended PiSSA/CorDA workflow; the quantisation half-step of LoftQ for $t\ge2$, with $W_{\rm res}=W-\delta(q_{t-1})$): defect $\kappa(W_{\rm res})-W_{\rm res}$;
- *quantise, then fit the error* (LoftQ with one iteration, HF's default `loftq_iter=1`; HF `replace_lora_weights_loftq`): HF sets the factors from $\mathrm{SVD}_r(W-\kappa W)$ without dividing by the LoRA scale $s$ ($\alpha/r$, or $\alpha/\sqrt r$ under rsLoRA), unlike its PiSSA and OLoRA inits, so $\delta_0=-s\,\mathrm{SVD}_r(e)$ and the defect is $e-s\,\mathrm{SVD}_r(e)$, with $\|e-s\,\mathrm{SVD}_r(e)\|^2=\|e-\mathrm{SVD}_r(e)\|^2+(1-s)^2\|\mathrm{SVD}_r(e)\|^2$. It is $e$ minus its best rank-$r$ approximation (rank $\operatorname{rank}e-r$) iff $s=1$, HF's bare default $r=\alpha=8$; for $s=2$ its norm equals $\|e\|$, no better than QLoRA. With a callback, `replace_lora_weights_loftq` can roll a module back to the zero init, whose defect is $e$;
- *quantise, split, re-quantise* (HF `olora_init` on bitsandbytes weights): defect $e+\kappa(r')-r'$ with $r'=\kappa W-\delta_0$.

Quantise-then-split has defect exactly $e$ iff the frozen part equals $\kappa W-\delta_0$, for instance $\kappa W$ kept quantised minus a frozen copy of the rank-$r$ $\delta_0$, at a cost of about $r(m+n)$ extra numbers. Re-quantising the residual, as HF `olora_init` does, generically adds $\kappa(r')-r'$.

Action families whose pointing does not depend on the base (OFT at $R=I$, BOFT at $(R,s)=(I,\mathbf 1)$, HiRA at $B=0$), evaluated at $\kappa\theta_0$, simply carry the defect $e$. Methods whose pointing is computed from the base have an order ambiguity of their own: DoRA's magnitude initialised from $\kappa\theta_0$ gives defect $e$, while initialised from $\theta_0$ it gives $\mathrm{diag}(\|w_{0,i}\|/\|(\kappa\theta_0)_i\|)\,\kappa\theta_0-\theta_0$. For action families a base change also moves the absolute invariants, not only the base point: NF4's exact zero code enlarges the zero set that HiRA must preserve, and exactly orthogonal (exact-Cayley) OFT preserves the Gram matrix of $\kappa\theta_0$ rather than that of $\theta_0$; HF's default Cayley–Neumann OFT preserves it only approximately.

(c) LoftQ alternates two updates on $\|\theta_0-Q-LR\|$: an exact rank-$r$ SVD step, and a round-to-nearest quantisation step with blockwise scales recomputed from its input. The second is not an exact projection, so the objective need not decrease monotonically. With $s=1$ the output is pointed up to the attained residual: an approximate section, meaning a choice $(Q,q_0)$ with reduced $\|\rho(q_0)-\theta_0\|$. In general HF's deployed defect after $T$ iterations is $(Q_T+L_TR_T-W)+(s-1)L_TR_T$, because HF's internal residual also omits $s$. The official LoftQ checkpoints use $r=64$ and $\alpha=16$, so $s=1/4$, and then the deployed defect can grow with $T$ while the attained residual falls.

(d) For a generic high-precision adapter, "fine-tune then quantise" and "quantise then fine-tune" do not commute. The first lands on the quantisation grid. In the second, the exactly merged weight $\kappa\theta_0+\Delta$ leaves the quantised type. For a uniform fixed-scale INT-$k$ grid, $\kappa\theta_0+\Delta$ stays on the grid iff $\Delta$ lies on the scale lattice (within range), so there the obstruction is the off-grid update. NF4 is non-uniform and not closed under addition, and absmax grids whose scales are recomputed are not closed either, so for QLoRA's NF4 the grid itself is part of the obstruction. Type-preserving merges, such as HF PEFT's dequantise–add–requantise for bitsandbytes 4/8-bit layers, re-quantise with recomputed block scales, so they stay in the quantised type but are lossy. QA-LoRA is the structured exception: its group-pooled adapter is constant on each quantisation group and merges into the zero-points, so the merged model stays INT-$k$.
proof: *Proof.* (a) is the definition of additivity. (b) Compute $\rho(q_0)-W$ in each pipeline: $\kappa(W_{\rm res})+\delta_0-W$ with $W=W_{\rm res}+\delta_0$; $\kappa W-s\,\mathrm{SVD}_r(e)-W$, whose norm follows from the Frobenius orthogonality of $\mathrm{SVD}_r(e)$ and $e-\mathrm{SVD}_r(e)$; and $\kappa(r')+\delta_0-W$. For DoRA, $\rho(q_0)=\mathrm{diag}(\mu_0/\|(\kappa\theta_0)_i\|)\,\kappa\theta_0$. (c) By construction; the failure of monotonicity is observed numerically. (d) In general $\kappa(\theta_0+\Delta)\ne\kappa\theta_0+\Delta$; a group-constant $\Delta$ is absorbed into the affine zero-points. ∎ [Num: on a $256\times256$ NF4 example whose weight has a dominant low-rank part, with $r=8$, $\|e\|=5.65$, QPiSSA's defect is $1.45$, LoftQ's ($T=1$, $s=1$) is $5.22$, and the LoftQ objective rises in $27$ of $60$ half-steps; on a Gaussian weight all three defects are close to $\|e\|$, and with $s=2$ the one-step LoftQ defect equals $\|e\|$ exactly; adding an NF4-representable update to an NF4 weight leaves the NF4 grid in most entries.]
referee_notes: (a) confirmed. Refuted: LoftQ's initial step was misclassified (LoftQ quantises first and fits the error, with defect (I - P_r)e); 'quantise-then-split has defect e' holds only with a high-precision residual (HF olora_init re-quantises); DoRA has an order ambiguity of its own (base-derived magnitude); LoftQ's alternation is not a monotone minimisation; (d)'s reason was wrong (uniform grids are closed under + within range; the obstruction is the off-grid update), and QA-LoRA is an exception. Repaired: a three-order classification with defects; base-derived pointings and moved invariants; (c) and (d) rewritten; added that QLoRA's image misses theta0 unless rank e <= r.
round2_notes: Round 2 (math refuted, major; faithful refuted, major): the core formulas hold. False: HF's LoftQ (loftq_init, replace_lora_weights_loftq) never divides by the LoRA scale s, so delta_0 = -s SVD_r(e) and the defect is e - s SVD_r(e), equal to the rank-r tail only for s = 1; with alpha = 2r it is as large as e, and for the official LoftQ checkpoints (s = 1/4) the deployed defect grows with T while the attained residual falls. Repaired: (b) and (c) restated with s, the Pythagorean norm formula and the general deployed defect; 'only if kept in high precision' replaced by the exact iff (a frozen copy of delta_0 keeps the memory saving); OFT's Gram statement restricted to exact Cayley; BOFT pointed at (I, 1); (d) distinguishes uniform fixed-scale grids (closed, obstruction is the off-grid update) from NF4 and recomputed-scale absmax grids (not closed); callback rollback noted; 'heuristic' and 'small' corrected; 'rank-r tail' rephrased. Knock-on: Thm II.1's defect sentence, the LoftQ worked example and the periodic-table row; Exposé 0 item 4 softened. Num states the test matrix structure, and an NF4 check is added to framework_checks.py.
public_statement: Quantising the frozen base moves the base point. QLoRA is ordinary LoRA anchored at the quantised weight $\kappa W$, so at initialisation it misses the pretrained $W$ by the generically full-rank quantisation error $e=\kappa W-W$, and it can reach $W$ only if $\operatorname{rank}e\le r$. Splitting or error-fitting initialisations change this defect in an order-dependent way: split-then-quantise (QPiSSA, HF's PiSSA/CorDA workflow) leaves $\kappa(W_{\rm res})-W_{\rm res}$; one-step LoftQ leaves $e-s\,\mathrm{SVD}_r(e)$, which is $e$ minus its best rank-$r$ approximation only when the LoRA scale $s=\alpha/r$ is $1$, because HF's LoftQ init ignores the scale; quantise-split-requantise (HF OLoRA on bitsandbytes weights) leaves $e+\kappa(r')-r'$. Exactly merging a high-precision adapter into a quantised base leaves the quantised type, and type-preserving merges are lossy, apart from group-constant adapters such as QA-LoRA under affine group quantisation.

name: rebasing closure
statement:
**Theorem V.3 (rebasing closure).** [Thm]

(a) *Additive methods with a fixed shape $C\ni0$*, with frames, masks and compression operators frozen at $\theta_0$ across cycles. $R_K=\theta_0+C^{+K}$, the $K$-fold Minkowski sum, and $R_\infty=\theta_0+\mathrm{Mon}(C)$, the additive monoid generated by $C$. If $C$ is closed under real scalings, $R_\infty=\theta_0+\mathrm{span}\,C$.

(b) *Action methods with $e\in S\subseteq G$*, or $\mathrm{id}\in S\subseteq\mathrm{End}(\Theta)$ for scaling methods. $R_K=S^K\theta_0$, and $R_\infty$ is the orbit of the generated monoid. Suppose $S$ lies in the subgroup generated by connected Lie subgroups $H_1,\dots,H_p$ and contains a neighbourhood of $e$ in each. Then the monoid generated by $S$ is the connected Lie subgroup $H$ with $\mathrm{Lie}(H)=\mathrm{Lie}\langle\mathfrak h_1,\dots,\mathfrak h_p\rangle$.

(c) *Block-orthogonal factors.* Let the factors have coordinate blocks $I_j\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ (block OFT, BOFT factors, Givens planes). Then $\mathrm{Lie}\langle\mathfrak{so}(I_j)\rangle=\bigoplus_C\mathfrak{so}(C)$, summed over the connected components $C$ of the hypergraph $(\{1..n\},\{I_j\})$.

*Corollaries.*
1. **ReLoRA.** $R_K=W_0+\mathcal M_{\le\min(Kr,m,n)}$. It reaches full fine-tuning iff $K\ge\lceil\min(m,n)/r\rceil$.
2. **Idempotent methods** gain nothing from rebasing: those whose shape is exactly a subspace, subgroup or submonoid independent of the base, with frames, masks and compression operators frozen across cycles. Examples: LoRA-FA with a fixed $A$, LoRA-XS with frozen frames, MoRA with fixed operators, FourierFT with fixed indices, WaveFT, C3A, MiSS (default balance mode; bat mode is base-dependent but still idempotent, since its blockwise maps $W\mapsto(W+I)(I+M)-I$ form a monoid), SHiRA, BitFit, FISH with a fixed mask, LN-tuning, (IA)$^3$, SSF, RoAd. Block OFT with a fixed partition and an exact Cayley map gains only the measure-zero set of block rotations with an eigenvalue $-1$: $R_\infty=W_0\cdot\prod SO(b)=\overline{R_1}$. Constrained OFT (COFT, an $\varepsilon$-ball) with an exact Cayley map gains up to $\prod SO(b)$; HF's `coft=True` keeps the Cayley–Neumann map by default and so falls under corollary 4. Methods that recompute frames or masks from the merged weight (an SVD-recomputing LoRA-XS, ReMoRA's alternating operators, resampled indices) do gain.
3. **VeRA.** $\mathrm{VeRA}^\infty=\text{LoRA-FA}(A)$ whenever the frozen $B$ has no zero entries.
4. **OFT family.** Block OFT with an exact Cayley map is stuck in $W_0\cdot\prod SO(b)$. HF's default Cayley–Neumann factor $R=C(Q)(I-Q^4)$ is not orthogonal: $R^\top R=(I-Q^4)^2$, with singular values $\lvert1-\mu_k^4\rvert$, where $\pm i\mu_k$ are the eigenvalues of $Q$. In the operating regime $\lVert Q\rVert_{\rm op}\le2^{1/4}$ every factor is a contraction, so re-merging decreases $K_{\rm out}$ in the Loewner order and lowers every singular value: the drift is monotone shrinkage, and the reachable set lies in $W_0$ times the block contraction semigroup. With unconstrained $Q$ the factors include singular ones ($\mu_k=1$), and re-merging generates $\prod\big(GL^+(b)\cup\mathcal M_{\le b-2}\big)$, or $\prod\big(CO^+(2)\cup\{0\}\big)$ when $b=2$ [Sketch]. Iterated BOFT with $m'$ butterfly factors of block size $b$ reaches $\mathrm{diag}(\mathbb R^m)\cdot W_0\cdot P\big(\prod SO(b\,2^{m'-1})\big)P^\top$, because the factor hypergraph has components of size $b\,2^{m'-1}$. This is $\mathrm{diag}(\mathbb R^m)\cdot W_0\cdot SO(n)$ iff $b\,2^{m'-1}=n$, the full-depth butterfly $m'=1+\log_2(n/b)$. HF's default `boft_n_butterfly_factor=1` is block OFT times $\mathrm{diag}(s)$. A *single* full-depth BOFT has dimension at most $m'\tfrac nb\binom b2<\dim SO(n)$ when $m'(b-1)<n-1$: it is a dense *matrix*, not a dense *set*.
5. **Re-HRA**, with $W_0$ injective, $r$ even and `apply_GS=False`. $R_K=(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le Kr})\cap W_0\cdot SO(n)$: *rebasing commutes with the meet*. This is the multiplicative twin of ReLoRA, and it reaches $W_0\cdot SO(n)$ in at most $\lceil n/r\rceil$ cycles.
6. **GaLore (with a gradient-SVD or a random projector), LISA and MeZO**, under the optimizer hypotheses of Prop IV.2, are rebasing schemes of *linear* methods whose shape moves. That is why they reach all of $\Theta$, while a fixed linear shape $L$ reaches only $\theta_0+L$ (corollary 2). Low rank is the per-period obstruction only for GaLore; LISA and MeZO already make full-rank per-matrix updates and gain coverage. Flora proper takes full-space steps with a compressed momentum, so it has no per-period low-rank shape.
7. **Merging never rescues an exactly orthogonal method from its absolute invariants.** In exact arithmetic, every exactly orthogonal input-side rebasing preserves $K_{\rm out}$ and the spectrum, and every output-side one preserves $K_{\rm in}$ and the spectrum (Cor II.6).
proof:
*Proof.* (a) follows by induction. If $C=\mathbb RC$, the monoid generated by $C$ contains $-C$ and is closed under scaling, so it is the span.

(b) Any neighbourhood of $e$ contains a symmetric one, and a symmetric neighbourhood of $e$ in a connected group generates that group as a monoid. The subgroup generated by connected Lie subgroups is the connected Lie subgroup with the generated Lie algebra (Yamabe).

(c) Write $L_{ab}=E_{ab}-E_{ba}$. Then $[L_{ac},L_{cb}]=L_{ab}$ for distinct $a,b,c$. Overlapping hyperedges therefore generate $\mathfrak{so}$ of their union, and $\bigoplus_C\mathfrak{so}(C)$ is a subalgebra that contains every generator.

The corollaries:
- (1) Rank is subadditive, and an SVD splits into blocks.
- (2) The exact Cayley image is dense and open in $SO(b)$, and every element of $SO(b)$ is a product of two elements of it.
- (3) The entries of $\Lambda_bB\Lambda_d$ are $b_iB_{ij}d_j$. Their span over $(b,d)$ is all of $\mathbb R^{m\times r}$ when every $B_{ij}\ne0$ (take $b=e_i$, $d=e_j$).
- (4) Apply (c) to the butterfly blocks. For the Cayley–Neumann factors, $C(Q)$ is orthogonal and commutes with $Q^4$, so the singular values of $R$ are $\lvert1-\mu_k^4\rvert\le1$ when $\lVert Q\rVert_{\rm op}\le2^{1/4}$, and $\det R=\prod_k(1-\mu_k^4)^2\ge0$. A product of contractions is a contraction, and $WR^\top RW^\top\preceq WW^\top$. The generated Lie algebra is $\mathfrak{gl}(b)$, but that identifies only the generated group: (b) does not apply, since the factors form a $\binom b2$-dimensional set containing no neighbourhood of $e$ in any connected subgroup. For the monoid, $R(Q)R(-Q)=(I-Q^4)^2$ gives positive pair-scalings, $R(Q)\lvert I-Q^4\rvert^{-1}$ gives $SO(b)$, the $KAK$ decomposition then gives $GL^+(b)$, and singular factors give $\mathcal M_{\le b-2}$.
- (5) "$\subseteq$" holds because $R_1R_2-I=R_1(R_2-I)+(R_1-I)$, so ranks add. Split them into $K$ consecutive groups of even size at most $r$, pad each group with pairs $H_uH_u$, and observe that each group is an HRA$_r$ element.

name: combination rules: gauge and naturality
statement:
**Proposition V.4 (combination rules: gauge and naturality).** [Prop]

(a) A rule $\Phi((B_i,A_i)_i)$ for combining LoRA factors descends to a function of the adapters $(B_iA_i)_i$ iff it is constant on the fibres of $(B_i,A_i)\mapsto(B_iA_i)$. On the full-rank locus this is equivalent to $\prod_iGL_r$-invariance. It is also equivalent for $\Phi$ continuous on the whole factor space [Sketch: each fibre contains a unique closed orbit, which lies in the closure of every orbit of the fibre].
- Task arithmetic $\sum w_is_iB_iA_i$ ($s_i$ is HF's `scaling`, $\alpha_i/r_i$, or $\alpha_i/\sqrt{r_i}$ under rsLoRA; HF's `cat` with merged scale $1$, Obs I.7) is invariant and lands in $\mathrm{LoRA}_{\sum_ir_i}$.
- LoraHub's factor-wise rule $(\sum w_iB_i)(\sum w_jA_j)$ is not invariant. Replacing $(B_2,A_2)$ by $(cB_2,A_2/c)$ changes it by $\sum_{l\ne2}w_lw_2\big[(c-1)B_2A_l+(c^{-1}-1)B_lA_2\big]$. HF's `add_weighted_adapter(..., combination_type="linear")` is a factor-wise rule of the same type: it weights $A_i$ by $\mathrm{sign}(w_i)\sqrt{\lvert w_is_i\rvert}$ and $B_i$ by $\sqrt{\lvert w_is_i\rvert}$ and sums the factors separately, so it has cross terms. On adapters that share a frozen $A$ it is still not exact up to a global factor, since the relative weights become $\sqrt{\lvert w_is_i\rvert}$. HF's non-SVD `ties`, `dare_*` and `magnitude_prune` variants also act on factors; the `*_svd` variants act on full updates.
- Poly and MHR are different. Their skill inventories are trained jointly through the product-of-sums map, which is invariant under the diagonal $GL_r$. For fixed generic routing with fewer skills than tasks and full-rank factors, this is the whole continuous fibre [Num]. With at least as many skills as tasks, or once the routing is counted as a parameter, there are further symmetries (skill permutations, and re-mixings $\alpha\mapsto\alpha M$ with $M\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1$). Their cross terms are a design choice, not an ill-definedness.

(b) *Well-definedness versus exactness.* A joint gauge fixing makes a factor-wise rule well defined. For rank-preserving product-of-sums rules, exactness for all weights $w$ needs degree one in $w$, which for injective factors forces a shared factor; `cat`, which concatenates and raises the rank, is exact without one. A frozen shared factor (FFA-LoRA; LoRA-FA) gives $(\sum w_iB_i)A=\sum w_iB_iA$ exactly. LoraHub with a shared $A$ still returns $(\sum_jw_j)\sum_iw_iB_iA$, exact only up to the global factor $\sum_jw_j$, since its weights are unnormalised. A per-module SVD canonical form leaves a $(\mathbb Z/2)^r$ of sign flips per module, plus rotations within repeated singular values, and these change the cross terms. What is needed is a *joint* frame that produces a shared factor, as KnOTS's joint re-factorisation of the concatenated updates through a shared $U\Sigma$ does. Federated LoRA shows the difference: FedAvg-LoRA clients start each round from the same broadcast $(B,A)$, so their failure, $\tfrac12(B_1+B_2)\cdot\tfrac12(A_1+A_2)\ne\tfrac12(B_1A_1+B_2A_2)$, is bilinearity, and it persists in a fully fixed gauge.

(c) *Naturality.* Task arithmetic is $GL(\Theta)$-equivariant on updates. DARE is coordinatewise and magnitude-free: $D(m\odot\tau)=m\odot(D\tau)$ for every invertible diagonal $D$ and the same mask $m$. So DARE is exactly equivariant under the torus $T_N$, sign flips included, for each mask, and under permutations in distribution; its distributional group is exactly $\mathrm{Mon}_N$. TIES with global trimming (top-$k$ magnitude, sign election by total mass as in the TIES paper and HF's default `"total"`, disjoint mean) is equivariant under $\mathbb R^\times\cdot B_N$, homotheties times signed permutations, generically (off magnitude ties at the threshold). With HF's `majority_sign_method="frequency"`, count ties are broken to $+1$ and the group drops to $\mathbb R_{>0}\cdot S_N$. Per-tensor trimming changes the group to $\prod_b(\mathbb R^\times\cdot B_{N_b})$, extended by permutations of equal-size blocks. DARE followed by full TIES (with trimming) is $\mathbb R^\times\cdot B_N$-equivariant in distribution; HF's and MergeKit's `dare_ties` has no magnitude trim, so with `"total"` election it is exactly $T_N$-equivariant per mask, and its group contains $\mathrm{Mon}_N$. None of the sparsifying rules (DARE, TIES, DARE-TIES) is $O(N)$-equivariant. Applied to factors and summed across adapters (HF's non-SVD variants), all of them are gauge-dependent: under independent per-adapter gauges even DARE fails, through the cross terms of (a). DARE's masking commutes with $T_r$ exactly for each mask and with $\mathrm{Mon}_r$ in distribution, so a single masked adapter, or a factor-wise sum under one gauge shared by all adapters, is $T_r$-invariant per mask and $\mathrm{Mon}_r$-invariant in distribution.
proof:
*Proof.* (a) On the full-rank locus, the fibres of $(B_i,A_i)\mapsto(B_iA_i)$ are $\prod GL_r$-orbits (Thm II.2). Off it, invariance alone is not enough: the projector onto $\mathrm{row}\,A$ is $GL_r$-invariant on $\{\operatorname{rank}A=r\}$, yet it differs at $(0,A)$ and $(0,A')$, which have the same product. Expand the LoraHub product. For Poly/MHR, if $\mathrm{col}\,B_i\cap\mathrm{col}\,B_j=0$ and the routing mixes skills $i$ and $j$, invariance of the cross term under per-skill gauges $g_i,g_j$ forces $B_i(g_i^{-1}g_j-I)A_j=0$, hence $g_i=g_j$.

(b) Flipping column $j$ of $B_i$ together with row $j$ of $A_i$ preserves the SVD form, and changes $B_iA_l$ for $l\ne i$.

(c) Masks and the rescaling by $1/(1-p)$ commute with diagonal maps, and an i.i.d. mask is permutation-invariant in law. Trimming by magnitude, electing signs by total mass and taking disjoint means commute with signed coordinate permutations and with $c\cdot I$ for $c\ne0$; with count-based election, ties have positive probability and are broken to $+1$, which is not sign-symmetric. Per-tensor trimming commutes with an independent homothety on each block. A rotation changes the magnitudes of individual coordinates. On factors, the all-ones mask has positive probability, and on it factor-wise DARE is the factor-wise rule of (a) times $(1-p)^{-2}$, so a per-adapter torus gauge changes it. ∎ [Num: DARE with a random non-unit diagonal $D$ is equivariant to $2\times10^{-15}$ per mask; TIES is homogeneous to $9\times10^{-16}$ and fails by $5.6$ under a generic positive diagonal; the general LoraHub change formula matches at $N=3$ to $2\times10^{-15}$; factor-wise DARE changes by $O(1)$ under a diagonal gauge on one adapter and by $10^{-15}$ under one shared by all adapters; for Poly with $3$ skills, $r=2$ and $6\times6$ weights, the fibre has dimension $32$ with $2$ tasks and $4=\dim GL_2$ with $4$ tasks.]
referee_notes: Core message confirmed. Refuted clauses: the 'iff' in (a) needs the full-rank locus (or continuity); the LoraHub change formula held only for N = 2; (c)'s groups were wrong: DARE is exactly torus-equivariant per mask (group containing Mon_N) and TIES is equivariant under homotheties times signed permutations, and 'only' was unproved. Also: HF's 'linear' combination is a LoraHub-type factor-wise rule; Poly and MHR are trained jointly (diagonal GL_r symmetry, not ill-defined); FedAvg's failure is bilinearity, not gauge; the [Pred] wrongly cited III.7(b). All repaired.
round2_notes: Round 2 (math refuted, major; faithful refuted, major): (a), (b) and the DARE/TIES full-update groups hold. False: 'applied to factors, DARE remains invariant under the monomial sub-gauge Mon_r' (under per-adapter gauges the cross terms change it; only a gauge shared by all adapters, or a single adapter, is invariant). Also wrong or loose: DARE-TIES as HF/MergeKit implement it has no magnitude trim and is T_N-equivariant per mask; per-tensor trimming enlarges rather than restricts the group (block scalars, equal-size block swaps); TIES's group needs total-mass sign election (HF 'frequency' drops to R_{>0} S_N); Poly/MHR's 'only symmetry is diagonal GL_r' needs fixed generic routing with fewer skills than tasks. Repaired: (c) rewritten with these groups and a proof of the factor-level failure; Poly/MHR statement qualified with a proof line; LoRA_{Nr} -> LoRA_{sum r_i}; s_i is HF's scaling (rsLoRA too); HF linear with a shared A is not exact up to a global factor; exactness restricted to rank-preserving product-of-sums rules (cat is exact); KnOTS called a joint re-factorisation; 'none is O(N)-equivariant' restricted to the sparsifying rules. Num extended and backed by framework_checks.py.
public_statement: A rule for combining LoRA factors is a well-defined function of the adapters $B_iA_i$ exactly when it is constant on the factorisation fibres; on the full-rank locus, or for continuous rules, that means invariance under each adapter's own $GL_r$ gauge. Task arithmetic on the products (HF's `cat` and `svd` merges) qualifies. Post-hoc product-of-sums rules (LoraHub, and HF's `linear` and non-SVD `ties`/`dare_*` merges) do not, because their cross terms change when a single adapter is rescaled; for rank-preserving rules exactness needs a shared factor, such as a common frozen $A$ or KnOTS's joint $U\Sigma$. On full updates, task arithmetic is $GL$-equivariant, DARE is equivariant under every invertible coordinate rescaling for each mask and under permutations in distribution, and TIES with sign election by total mass is equivariant under homotheties times signed permutations; none of the sparsifying rules is rotation-equivariant.

name: the activation fixes the privileged basis
statement:
**Lemma VI.2 (the activation fixes the privileged basis).** [Lemma; classical: Sussmann 1992; Chen–Lu–Hecht-Nielsen 1993; Godfrey et al. 2022] Let $\sigma:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be an elementwise activation that is not affine, and let $L\in GL_d$ commute with it as maps on $\mathbb R^d$: $L\,\sigma^{\times d}=\sigma^{\times d}L$.

(a) If $\sigma\in C^2$, then $L=PD$ is monomial.

(b) If $\sigma$ is ReLU or leaky ReLU with slope $\alpha\ne1$, then $L=PD$ with $D$ a positive diagonal.

(c) If moreover $\sigma$ is real-analytic at $0$ with $\sigma(t)=\sum a_kt^k$, each diagonal entry $c$ of $D$ satisfies $ca_k=c^ka_k$ for all $k$. So $c=1$ for GELU and SiLU, since $\sigma''(0)\neq0$, and $c=\pm1$ for tanh.
proof:
*Proof.* (a) Fix row $i$; its row vector $\ell_i$ is nonzero because $L$ is invertible. The left side $\sum_jL_{ij}\sigma(x_j)$ has vanishing mixed partials $\partial_j\partial_k$ for $j\ne k$. The right side has mixed partial $L_{ij}L_{ik}\sigma''(\ell_i\cdot x)$. Choose $t_0$ with $\sigma''(t_0)\ne0$, which exists because $\sigma$ is not affine, and $x$ with $\ell_i\cdot x=t_0$. So $L_{ij}L_{ik}=0$: each row has a single nonzero entry.

(b) ReLU is not $C^2$, so argue by kinks instead. The left side of row $i$ is non-differentiable exactly on $\bigcup_{j:L_{ij}\ne0}\{x_j=0\}$, and the right side exactly on the hyperplane $\{\ell_i\cdot x=0\}$. The two sets are equal, and a hyperplane equal to a finite union of coordinate hyperplanes is one of them. So row $i$ has a single entry $L_{ij}$, and $L_{ij}\sigma(t)=\sigma(L_{ij}t)$ at $t=1$ forces $L_{ij}>0$. Leaky ReLU is identical.

(c) $P$ commutes with $\sigma^{\times d}$, so $D\sigma=\sigma D$, i.e. $c\,\sigma(t)=\sigma(ct)$; compare Taylor coefficients at $0$. ∎
referee_notes: Both referees: lemma true and classical. Wording fixes: standing hypotheses (sigma not affine, L in GL_d commuting as maps); leaky slope alpha != 1; Taylor coefficients at 0; proof steps (the choice of t0, both inclusions of the kink sets) made explicit; credited to Sussmann, Chen-Lu-Hecht-Nielsen and Godfrey et al. Commentary corrected: SwiGLU and GeGLU FFNs have the full monomial group, the LayerNorm-gain basis comes from the parametrisation, BOFT is equivariant on up and gate projections; the permutation [Pred] restated as a variance claim.
round2_notes: Not covered by round 2; round-1 status kept.
public_statement: An invertible linear map that commutes with a non-affine elementwise activation is a permutation times a diagonal for $C^2$ activations, a permutation times a positive diagonal for ReLU and leaky ReLU, a signed permutation for tanh, and a plain permutation for GELU and SiLU (Sussmann 1992; Chen–Lu–Hecht-Nielsen 1993). So the activation fixes a privileged neuron basis up to these symmetries.

name: the merge calculus
statement:
**Theorem VI.3 (the merge calculus).** [Thm; the rules are elementary, and the merge facts for (IA)$^3$ (Liu et al. 2022, Sec. 3.3), SSF (re-parameterisation) and LoRA (linearity) are known. Scale migration through SwiGLU, ReLU and norms, and the GELU obstruction, are used by AWQ (Lin et al. 2024) and SmoothQuant (Xiao et al. 2023). New: only the packaging as a merge calculus for PEFT, with explicit side conditions] Work with activation-side diagrams in a symmetric monoidal category of continuous, piecewise-smooth maps with copy and discard nodes. (We call copy and the Hadamard product "spiders" by analogy only; in this cartesian setting they do not satisfy the Frobenius law.) A *trainable box* is a node whose weight ranges over a stated class: all linear maps, or all affine maps when the box has a bias slot. R2 and R4–R7 are identities of maps; R1 is a closure property and R3 a characterisation.

| rule | statement | when it holds |
|---|---|---|
| R1 (fusion) | composites and parallel sums of linear (affine) boxes are linear (affine) | the operators involved are position-independent |
| R2 (permutation slide) | $P\sigma^{\times d}=\sigma^{\times d}P$ | every elementwise $\sigma$ |
| R3 (positive-diagonal slide) | $\mathrm{diag}(\ell)\sigma^{\times d}=\sigma^{\times d}\mathrm{diag}(\ell)$ for all $\ell\ge0$ | iff $\sigma$ is positively homogeneous (ReLU, leaky ReLU; not GELU, SiLU, tanh); such $\sigma$ are piecewise linear |
| R4 (spider slide) | $\mathrm{diag}(\ell)(a\odot b)=(\mathrm{diag}(\ell)a)\odot b$ | any $\ell$ |
| R5 (cup slide) | $\langle Mq,k\rangle=\langle q,M^\top k\rangle$ | always. Under RoPE, $\langle R_mMq,R_nk\rangle=\langle q,M^\top R_{n-m}k\rangle$ holds for every $M$, but the slide onto the key side, $\langle R_mMq,R_nk\rangle=\langle R_mq,R_nM^\top k\rangle$ for all $m,n$, holds iff $M^\top$ commutes with every $R_{n-m}$ that occurs; for diagonal $M$ and distinct frequencies, iff $\ell$ is constant on each rotary pair (in either pairing convention) |
| R6 (norm absorption) | $W(\gamma\odot n(x)+\beta)=(W\mathrm{diag}\gamma)\,n(x)+W\beta$ | always; the shift $W\beta$ needs a bias slot, and an RMSNorm gain has no $\beta$ |
| R7 (copy slide) | applying $D$ and then copying equals copying and then applying $D$ to every copy | always |

Consequences:

(a) **Affine edits.** Let a method insert a position-uniform affine edit $E_q$ on a wire $w$ of the base network $f$, for every $q\in Q$. Suppose every reader of $w$ is a trainable, unshared box (no weight tying) whose class is closed under precomposition with $E_q$; a shift needs a bias slot. Then the method merges, by $W_c\mapsto W_cE_q$ for all readers $c$ at once. Absorption into a box that the extension itself inserts does not count. Edits that violate these hypotheses fall outside (a), and R1–R7 do not merge them; whole-network non-mergeability is open (Exposé XI). Position-selective edits (ReFT/LoReFT, and position-gated LoRA variants such as Activated LoRA) are not box-locally mergeable. Residual-stream edits need case analysis: an edit merges into the box that produces the wire when that box can absorb it (an untied embedding table; for a fixed-position edit at layer $0$, a learned absolute positional table), a shift folds into a writer's bias when one exists, a diagonal edit after a post-LN folds into that LN's affine parameters, and an orthogonal edit in an RMSNorm model merges globally, SliceGPT/QuaRot-style. No merge is known for LoReFT's non-orthogonal low-rank edit.

(b) **Diagonal methods.** A diagonal method merges into a box reached by R1–R7 if all of the following hold: the rules move *every* copy of $\mathrm{diag}(\ell)$ into trainable boxes for all $\ell$ in the method's parameter domain (with $\ell\ge0$ when R3 is used); no position-dependent operator lies on the path (for RoPE, $\ell$ is constant on each rotary pair); the target box is unshared, or $\ell$ is constant across the sharing group; and every shift has a bias slot. Conversely, the RoPE condition is necessary for sliding a query scaling onto $W_K$ when $W_Q$ and $W_K$ have full rank and at least two occurring relative offsets have rotation angles that are not multiples of $\pi$. Without such genericity hypotheses the conditions are not necessary: a dead rotary pair, or zero entries of $\ell$ under ReLU, can still merge.

(c) **Non-affine edits.** For a linear or affine box, an edit whose modified box function is non-affine in the box input, for some parameter value, is not box-locally mergeable. For linear and affine boxes this is the definition; for non-linear boxes such as attention, see Thm VI.5(f).

(d) **Type relativity.** A generic high-precision update is off the quantisation grid, so exact merging of a QLoRA or LoftQ update leaves the quantised type, a type-preserving merge is lossy, and QA-LoRA's group-constant adapters are the exception (Prop V.2(d)).
proof: *Proof.* R2, R4, R5, R6 and R7 are identities; under RoPE, $R_m^\top R_n=R_{n-m}$ gives the first form of R5 for every $M$. For R3, $\ell\sigma(t)=\sigma(\ell t)$ for all $\ell\ge0$ and all $t$ is positive homogeneity of degree one, and a $C^1$ positively homogeneous $\sigma$ on $\mathbb R$ is linear. (a) The closure and reader conditions put $W_cE_q$ in each reader's class, R7 distributes $E_q$ to every reader, and position-uniformity lets one weight absorb the edit at every position. (b) The "if" direction is (a) applied at the box reached. For the RoPE converse, equality of all logits with full-rank $W_Q,W_K$ forces $R_\Delta^{-1}\mathrm{diag}(\ell)R_\Delta$ to be one matrix for every occurring offset $\Delta$, including $\Delta=0$, so $\mathrm{diag}(\ell)$ commutes with $R_\Delta$; on a rotary pair whose angle is not a multiple of $\pi$ this forces equal entries. (c) is the definition of box-local mergeability. (d) is Prop V.2(d). ∎ [Num: under RoPE, $\langle R_mMq,R_nk\rangle=\langle q,M^\top R_{n-m}k\rangle$ holds for a generic $M$ to $10^{-15}$ while the slide onto the key side fails; a query scaling slid onto $W_K$ leaves a $7.6\%$ least-squares residual unless $\ell$ is pair-constant; folding post-LN gains into $W_1$ changes the output; legal rewrites agree to $10^{-15}$.]

Refuted consequences: (a) contradicted the framework's own LoReFT analysis and fails for position-gated edits; (b) fails under GQA sharing, under RoPE (a query scaling does not slide onto W_K), under post-LN fan-out and for tied embeddings; affine shifts need bias slots; R3 is not a 'smooth' identity; (d)'s reason was wrong; 'the consequences are new' overclaimed. Repaired: a setting with copy spiders and trainable boxes (R7 copy slide added); (a)-(d) restated with side conditions (position-uniformity, unshared targets, bias slots, RoPE); corollaries corrected; prior work credited.

False: R5 under RoPE as written (<R_m M q, R_n k> = <q, M^T R_{n-m} k> holds for every M; the condition belongs to the slide onto the key side); (b)'s 'only if' was unproved and false without genericity (dead rotary pair; zero entries under ReLU); (a)'s blanket 'they are M-infinity' for residual-stream and extension edits was unproved and false (embedding fold, post-LN affine fold, bias fold, SliceGPT-style rotation; SSF and (IA)^3 themselves); 'new GLU/W_up observation' was already in AWQ's code. Repaired: R5 restated; (b) stated as sufficiency with a proved RoPE converse under genericity; (a)'s exclusion replaced by 'falls outside (a)' with a case analysis of residual-stream edits; GQA dropped from (a); R3 allows l >= 0; (d) says generic; AWQ and SmoothQuant credited; GELU non-fusion proved; RMSNorm gains fold without a bias slot; AdapterFusion stays M-infinity with a constant gate; 'not mergeable' is box-local; tied-weight caveat added; 'decided/decidable' changed to 'certified' here, in Exposé 0, rosetta.json, visuals.md and narrative.md.
public_statement: A few exact rewrite rules give sufficient conditions for folding a scaling or affine PEFT edit into existing weights with no change in output. They are linear fusion, permutation slides through any elementwise activation, positive-diagonal slides through positively homogeneous ones such as ReLU, diagonal slides through the linear branch of a GLU, transposition across the query–key product (under RoPE only for scalings constant on each rotary pair), norm-gain absorption and copying. The conditions are that the edit is the same at every position, the absorbing weights are unshared, and any shift has a bias slot. For example, (IA)$^3$'s FFN scale always folds into $W_{\rm down}$, and also into $W_{\rm up}$ under SwiGLU or GeGLU for every scale (a migration AWQ already uses) but not under GELU. Position-selective edits (ReFT, Activated LoRA) and nonlinear adapters are not box-locally mergeable, and exactly merging a generic QLoRA or LoftQ update leaves the quantised format, with QA-LoRA as the exception. This is a set of sufficient conditions plus box-local obstructions, not a decision procedure for whole-network mergeability.

name: linear insertions, and ReFT
statement:
**Proposition VI.4 (linear insertions, and ReFT).** [Prop]

(a) A linear adapter in parallel with a single linear box, $W_0x+sUDx$, *is* LoRA: it has the same $\rho$ (He et al. 2022, Table 1). A linear adapter parallel to a whole sublayer (He et al.'s parallel adapter around attention or the FFN) edits the weightless skip connection rather than a base box, and is not box-locally mergeable when the sublayer is non-affine.

(b) Let $W_0\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ be bias-free (as LLaMA-type $W_o$ and $W_{\rm down}$ are), and $r\ge1$. A serial linear adapter after $W_0$, $(I+UD)W_0$ with $U\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}$ and $D\in\mathbb R^{r\times m}$ (scale absorbed), has image $W_0+\{Y\in\mathcal M_{\le r}:\mathrm{row}\,Y\subseteq\mathrm{row}\,W_0\}$. It is expressively equivalent to LoRA iff $\operatorname{rank}W_0=n$, and weakly (unpointed) isomorphic to LoRA iff $W_0$ is invertible. The isomorphism $(U,D)\mapsto(U,DW_0)$ sends a base point $(U_0,D_0)$ to $(U_0,D_0W_0)$. For a fixed $\mathrm T_A$ pointing $(0,A_0)$ with $\operatorname{rank}A_0=r$ and $1\le r<m=n$, a pointed isomorphism exists iff $W_0$ is invertible and $\mathrm{row}\,A_0=\mathrm{row}(D_0W_0)$, and then $U_0=0$ automatically. With a bias $b_0$, the serial adapter also moves the bias by $UDb_0$, so on the affine box its image differs from weight-only LoRA's. Houlsby's near-identity initialisation (weights from $\mathcal N(0,10^{-2})$, truncated) makes practical serial adapters slightly unpointed; the pointed statement applies to zero-up initialisations.

(c) LoReFT (Wu et al. 2024) is $\Phi(h)=h+R^\top(Wh+b-Rh)$, with $R\in\mathbb R^{r\times d}$ having orthonormal rows, applied at selected positions. On one hidden vector it is the extension by an **identity box** followed by a rank-$\le r$ affine edit,
$$\Phi(h)=(I+R^\top(W-R))h+R^\top b,$$
which is LoRA$_r$ on the *affine* identity box $[I_d\mid0]$ in homogeneous coordinates, with $B=R^\top$ constrained to the Stiefel manifold and $A=[W-R\mid b]$. Its image is $(I,0)+\mathcal M_{\le r}(d\times(d+1))$, of dimension $r(2d+1-r)$. The bias is confined to $\mathrm{col}\,B$, so for $r<d$ this is not LoRA$_r$ $\oplus$ BitFit, whose dimension is larger by $d-r$. It is simulated, through $h(R,W,b)=(R^\top,[W-R\mid b])$, by LoRA$_r$ on that affine box pointed at $(R_0^\top,0)$, a $\mathrm T_B$ pointing with $\mathrm{col}\,B_0=\mathrm{row}\,R_0$; this homogeneous-coordinate LoRA has a bias column in $A$, unlike HF LoRA. It is not simulated by $\mathrm T_A$-pointed LoRA$_r$, since its $\dim S_1=r(d+1)$ exceeds $rd$. It is not isomorphic to LoRA$_r$: its parameter count is smaller by $r(r+1)/2$, and its residual symmetry is $O(r)$, acting by $(R,W,b)\mapsto(OR,OW,Ob)$. It is pointed iff $W=R$ and $b=0$. The reference implementation (pyreft) initialises $W$ and $b$ by the default `nn.Linear` init, independently of $R$, so practical LoReFT has a pointing defect $R^\top((W_0-R_0)h+b_0)$: at initialisation it replaces the $R$-component of $h$ by a random affine function, and the simulation above is then only a weak morphism. pyreft also applies dropout to the whole output, $h$ included, so the training-time map is not $\Phi$.
proof: *Proof.* (a) holds by definition; a sublayer-parallel adapter adds $sUDx$ to $F(x)$ for a non-affine sublayer $F$, and no base weight sees $x$ linearly. (b) $UDW_0$ ranges over the rank-$\le r$ matrices whose rows lie in $\mathrm{row}W_0$, which is all of $\mathcal M_{\le r}$ iff $\mathrm{row}W_0=\mathbb R^n$. If $W_0$ is invertible, $(U,D)\mapsto(U,DW_0)$ is a linear bijection over $\Theta$. Conversely, an isomorphism preserves $\mathrm{Im}$ (Obs I.4(c)), forcing $\operatorname{rank}W_0=n$, and is a diffeomorphism, forcing $2mr=r(m+n)$, i.e. $m=n$. Pointed case, "if": pointedness gives $U_0D_0W_0=0$, so $U_0D_0=0$; $\operatorname{rank}D_0=r$ then forces $U_0=0$, and composing $(U,D)\mapsto(U,DW_0)$ with the gauge $g\in GL_r$ with $A_0=gD_0W_0$ gives the pointed isomorphism. "Only if": the unpointed part gives $W_0$ invertible, and Obs I.6 gives $\{XD_0W_0+U_0Y\}=\{Z:\mathrm{row}\,Z\subseteq\mathrm{row}\,A_0\}$; since $r<n$, a nonzero $U_0$ would produce some $U_0Y$ with a row outside $\mathrm{row}\,A_0$, so $U_0=0$ and the row spaces agree. With a bias, $(I+UD)(W_0x+b_0)=(W_0+UDW_0)x+b_0+UDb_0$. (c) Expand. Every $d\times(d+1)$ matrix of rank $\le r$ factors as $R^\top V$ with $R^\top$ having orthonormal columns (QR), so the image is as stated. $R^\top$ is injective, so the edit vanishes iff $W=R$ and $b=0$. Finally, $R^\top O^\top(OW-OR)=R^\top(W-R)$. The parameter count is $rd-\tfrac{r(r+1)}2+rd+r$ against $r(2d+1)$, and at the neutral point $S_1=\{R_0^\top V\}$ has dimension $r(d+1)$. ∎ [Num: Jacobian rank $22=r(2d+1-r)$ at $d=6$, $r=2$, against $26$ for LoRA$_r$ $\oplus$ bias; serial-adapter image dimension $7$ at $(m,n,r)=(5,3,1)$ and at $(4,8,1)$, against $11$ for LoRA at $(4,8,1)$.]

public_statement: For a bias-free linear layer $W_0\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, a linear adapter in parallel with $W_0$ is exactly LoRA, and a linear serial adapter $(I+UD)W_0$ reaches exactly the rank-$\le r$ updates whose rows lie in $\mathrm{row}\,W_0$. That set equals LoRA's reachable set iff $\operatorname{rank}W_0=n$, and is a reparametrisation of LoRA iff $W_0$ is square and invertible. On each hidden vector, LoReFT (Wu et al. 2024) is a rank-$\le r$ affine edit of an inserted identity map, that is, LoRA on an affine identity box with its up-factor restricted to orthonormal columns. Its reachable set has dimension $r(2d+1-r)$ with the bias confined to the column space of $R^\top$, its residual symmetry is $O(r)$, and it is simulated by, but not isomorphic to, LoRA$_r$ pointed with $A_0=0$. With pyreft's default initialisation it is not the identity at step 0, and because it acts only at selected positions of the weightless residual stream it does not merge into the base weights.

name: attention is a homomorphism followed by a perspective map
statement:
**Theorem VI.5 (attention is a homomorphism followed by a perspective map).** [Thm; the identity is standard; (b) is due to He et al. 2022; (c) and the soft-prompt-to-prefix map in (e) are due to Petrov–Torr–Bibi 2024, §2.2 (informally Li–Liang 2021, §7.2); the monoid organisation, the explicit position hypotheses and the slice-category typing of (e) are ours] Fix a query $q$. Multisets of key–value pairs form a commutative monoid under $\uplus$. Define
$$\Sigma_q(K)=\Big(\sum e^{\langle q,k\rangle/\sqrt d},\ \sum e^{\langle q,k\rangle/\sqrt d}\,v\Big).$$
(a) $\Sigma_q$ is a monoid homomorphism into $(\mathbb R_{\ge0}\times\mathbb R^{d_v},+)$, landing in $\{Z>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\}$. On nonempty multisets, $\mathrm{Attn}_q=\pi\circ\Sigma_q$ with the partial map $\pi(Z,S)=S/Z$, defined for $Z>0$.

(b) **Prefix is a gated parallel adapter.** For nonempty $P$ and $C$, $\mathrm{Attn}_q(P\uplus C)=(1-\lambda_q)\mathrm{Attn}_q(C)+\lambda_q\mathrm{Attn}_q(P)$, with $\lambda_q=Z_q(P)/(Z_q(P)+Z_q(C))$.

(c) **Per-layer pattern rigidity.** Within a single layer, for fixed $q$ and a fixed content multiset $C$: the content attention weights are multiplied by $1-\lambda_q$, their ratios are unchanged, and the output lies on the segment from $\mathrm{Attn}_q(C)$ to $\mathrm{Attn}_q(P)\in\mathrm{conv}\,V_P$. This rigidity is relative to the same layer's computation without the prefix; it is relative to the pretrained pattern only at the lowest prefixed layer. Lower-layer prefixes change the queries and the content keys and values of higher layers, so attention patterns at the level of the network are *not* rigid (Petrov–Torr–Bibi 2024, §6; the same authors show that prefix-tuning a pretrained transformer can be a universal approximator, arXiv:2402.14753).

(d) **LLaMA-Adapter** normalises $P$ and $C$ separately and adds a zero-initialised gate: $\mathrm{Attn}_q(C)+\tanh(g_l)\,\mathrm{Attn}_q(P)$, with one gate per head in the paper; HF PEFT uses one raw zero-initialised scalar per layer, without $\tanh$. It uses two perspective maps, leaves the content weights exactly unchanged, and is pointed at $g=0$. Its prompt keys and values are the frozen $W_k,W_v$ applied to one learned prompt per adapted layer, and it acts in the top layers only.

(e) **Prompt $\to$ deep prefix in causal decoders.** Assume that the soft prompt comes first, that attention is causal, and that content positions are offset by the prompt length $m$ in both methods (as HF PEFT does via `cache_position`). Then at every layer the states at prompt positions depend only on $p$, and $h:p\mapsto(K_j(p),V_j(p))_j$ satisfies $\Phi\circ\rho_{\rm prefix}\circ h=\Phi\circ\rho_{\rm prompt}$ as functions of the content tokens, read at content positions. The two methods live on different extensions, so this is an arrow of the unpointed slice over the realisation $C^\infty(X_{\rm content},Y_{\rm content})$, not of $\mathsf{Meth}$. Under RoPE without the offset, a different $h$ works: rotate each prefix key by $-m$ (positions $-m,\dots,-1$). For additive relative biases (ALiBi, T5) the answer depends on how the implementation places the prefix keys. The construction does not apply in bidirectional encoders of depth $\ge2$.

(f) **Obstructions.** Call a head *standard* if it is vanilla softmax attention without torch-style `add_bias_kv` (which would absorb a one-token prefix), `add_zero_attn`, learned attention sinks or softmax-plus-one. On length-one contexts, every weight setting of a standard head is affine in $x$. Some prefix makes the prefixed head non-affine on length-one contexts iff $W_o\ne0$ and ($W_q\ne0$ or $W_k^\top b_q\ne0$); for bias-free heads, iff $W_o\ne0$ and $W_q\ne0$. For such frozen weights and generic prefixes the prefixed head is not affine, because the gate $\lambda(x)$ is not constant. So prefix tuning and P-tuning v2 are not box-locally mergeable into a standard head. When $W_oW_v\ne0$, no prefix is neutral, so prompt and prefix tuning are unpointed.
proof:
*Proof.* (a) Sums over a disjoint union split, and $Z=0$ only for the empty multiset.

(b) $\pi(Z_P+Z_C,S_P+S_C)=\lambda S_P/Z_P+(1-\lambda)S_C/Z_C$.

(c) Each content weight is $e^{\langle q,k\rangle/\sqrt d}/(Z_P+Z_C)=(1-\lambda)e^{\langle q,k\rangle/\sqrt d}/Z_C$, and $\mathrm{Attn}_q(P)$ is a convex combination of $V_P$.

(d) This is the definition.

(e) Induction over layers: under causal masking, prompt positions attend only to prompt positions, and with the stated offset their positional encodings agree in both methods. Without the offset under RoPE, prefix keys sit in the cache already rotated, so the content-to-prompt displacement changes unless each key is rotated back by $-m$.

(f) A softmax over one token equals $1$, so the original head computes $W_o(W_vx+b_v)+b_o$. With a prefix, the output is $(1-\lambda(x))W_o(W_vx+b_v)+\lambda(x)W_o\mathrm{Attn}_{q(x)}(P)+b_o$. If $W_o=0$ it is constant. If $W_q=0$ and $W_k^\top b_q=0$, every score is constant in $x$, so $\lambda$ is constant and the output is affine. Otherwise, take a ray $x=tu$ along which some score difference varies (with $W_qu\ne0$, or with the content score $\langle b_q,W_ktu\rangle$ varying), one prefix token whose key keeps the gate $\lambda(t)$ non-constant, and a value $v$ with $W_ov$ large. The gate is a bounded, non-constant analytic function of $t$, so $\lambda''\ne0$ somewhere, and for large $W_ov$ the term $\lambda(t)W_ov$ dominates the second difference. The prefixed output is real-analytic in $(x,\text{prefix})$, so this witness makes the prefixes with affine output a nowhere-dense analytic subset. Unpointedness: $\lambda(x)>0$ always, and a neutral prefix would need $W_o\mathrm{Attn}_{q(x)}(P)=W_o(W_vx+b_v)$ for all $x$; the left side lies in the compact set $W_o\,\mathrm{conv}\,V_P$, while the right side is unbounded when $W_oW_v\ne0$. ∎ [Num: on a 3-layer, 2-head causal decoder, prompt-to-prefix agreement is $9\times10^{-16}$ with RoPE and the offset, against $1.3$ without it and $2\times10^{-15}$ with keys rotated by $-m$; a head with $W_o=0$ stays affine although $W_q^\top W_k\ne0$, and one with $W_q\ne0$, $W_q^\top W_k=0$ does not (referee replication).]

public_statement:
For a fixed query, softmax attention is a monoid homomorphism into (normaliser, weighted value sum) followed by division. As a consequence, a prefix acts as an input-gated parallel adapter (He et al. 2022) that rescales, but never reorders, the content attention weights within its layer (Petrov–Torr–Bibi 2024), while LLaMA-Adapter's separate softmax with a zero-initialised gate leaves those weights unchanged and is the identity at initialisation. In causal decoders whose content positions are offset by the prompt length, every soft prompt is realised exactly by the deep prefix made of its own per-layer keys and values (Petrov–Torr–Bibi 2024; informally Li–Liang 2021). e0$ and $W_q
e0$, a generic prefix makes the head non-affine even on single-token inputs, so prefix tuning cannot be folded into the head's own weights, and when $W_oW_v
e0$ no prefix is neutral.
